Cinci suspecți din dosarul de infracțiuni cu violență săvârșite de o grupare din Brăila au fost arestați preventiv. DIICOT anunţă, sâmbătă, că magistraţii Curţii de Apel Bucureşti au admis propunerea procurorilor şi au dispus arestarea a cinci persoane în dosarul care vizează săvârşirea a numeroase infracţiuni cu violenţă de către o grupare care acţiona în Brăila. Încă din 2021, sub coordonarea unui bărbat de 50 de ani, gruparea a săvârşit numeroase infracţiuni cu violenţă. Cel puţin patru tentative de omor au fost instrumentate de către procurori, care precizează că victimele au supravieţuit independent de voinţa agresorilor.

Accident pe Valea Oltului, la Călimănești: două mașini s-au ciocnit, o victimă încarcerată, una pe asfalt. Traficul e blocat. Două maşini s-au ciocnit, sâmbătă, pe DN 7, în judeţul Vâlcea, două persoane fiind rănite. O victimă este încarcerată, iar cealaltă proiectată pe carosabil. Traficul este oprit la Călimăneşti.

Un avion F-35 s-a prăbușit lângă o bază militară din California: pilotul a reușit să se catapulteze. Un avion de vânătoare s-a prăbuşit, vineri, în apropierea unei baze militare din San Diego, California de Sud, au anunţat autorităţile americane.

Britanic arestat pentru spionaj în favoarea Iranului la baza RAF Akrotiri din Cipru: ce detalii ies la iveală. Un britanic a fost arestat sub suspiciunea de spionaj asupra unei baze militare britanice din Cipru în numele armatei iraniene, relatează BBC.

Complotul pentru achitarea lui Luigi Mangione: cum ar putea scăpa de închisoare americanul care a asasinat un director de asigurări. O particularitate a sistemului juridic american i-ar putea permite lui Luigi Mangione să scape nepedepsit — chiar dacă jurații îl consideră vinovat de uciderea unui director din domeniul asigurărilor de sănătate, iar experții afirmă că este o ofensă adusă justiției, dezvăluie The Times.

Probleme cu traficul pe Dunăre. Încărcătura navelor, redusă chiar și la jumătate din capacitate din cauza cotelor scăzute. Din cauza cotelor extrem de scăzute din luna iulie, apropiate de minimul istoric, navele care tranzitează Dunărea merg şi pe jumătate goale, pentru a-şi menţine capacitatea de plutire. Cele mai mari probleme sunt pe sectorul fluvial, unde nu-şi pot descărca nici marfa în unele porturi.

Mii de persoane sunt aşteptate la Amsterdam pentru un WorldPride, la o săptămână de la atentatul de la Berlin. Mii de participanţi se vor aduna sâmbătă de-a lungul canalelor din Amsterdam pentru evenimentul principal al WorldPride, care promite o sărbătoare LGBT plină de viaţă, despre care organizatorii spun că este deosebit de urgentă după atacul mortal de săptămâna trecută la marşul Pride din Berlin, potrivit Reuters.

SUA intenționează să lanseze noi atacuri asupra Iranului (The Hill). Potrivit unor informații, SUA ar intenționa să relanseze atacurile împotriva Iranului încă din acest weekend, au declarat vineri oficiali americani pentru mai multe surse media citate de The Hill.

Peste 48.000 de migranți s-au întors în Maroc din Ceuta, afirmă Spania. Măsuri de securitate înăsprite în Franța și Italia. Peste 48.000 de migranți s-au întors în Maroc din enclava spaniolă Ceuta, unde au sosit aproximativ 60.000 de persoane în ultimele zile, a anunțat vineri seara Ministerul de Interne al Spaniei, scrie 7sur7.be.

Nicușor Dan, apel către români: „Țara se stabilizează financiar și va fi mai bine; România funcționează”. Ce spune de trecerea la euro. Preşedintele Nicuşor Dan a transmis sâmbătă că, în ciuda zgomotului politic, România funcţionează, dintre legile importante mai fiind de adoptat doar Legea salarizării. Şeful statului a subliniat că va promulga sâptămâna viitoare ultimele legi adoptate de Parlament, care sunt jaloane în PNRR

Grindeanu anunță că Parlamentul a găsit bani pentru procesul legat de medalia olimpică a Anei Maria Bărbosu. Preşedintele PSD și președinte al Camerei Deputaților, Sorin Grindeanu, a anunţat, sâmbătă, că Parlamentul a găsit soluţia prin care asigurăm fondurile necesare pentru ca România să meargă până la capăt, la Lausanne, în procesul legat de medalia olimpică a Anei Maria Bărbosu

România, sub cupola de foc: cod roșu de caniculă pentru trei județe, de duminică. Zonele afectate și cât de cald va fi astăzi. Meteorologii anunţă că valul de caniculă se extinde şi se înteţeşte, fiind emisă o avertizare cod roşu, valabilă de duminică, pentru judeţele judeţele Satu Mare, Bihor şi Arad, unde temperaturile vor depăşi 40 de grade Celsius. Sâmbătă, în vestul, sud-vestul, centrul și nordul țării vor fi în vigoare un cod portocaliu și unul galben de caniculă.

De ce fug oamenii din Maroc: explicația crizei de la granița spaniolă. Migranții care caută o viață mai bună consideră Ceuta o poartă de acces către restul Europei — însă evenimentele din ultima săptămână au avut loc în urma unei noi hotărâri a Curții Supreme a Spaniei. Trecerea a mii de persoane din Maroc pe teritoriul spaniol a determinat mai multe țări din Uniunea Europeană să solicite suspendarea Spaniei din spațiul Schengen, scrie The Times.

Traian Băsescu, despre criza energetică: „Este un caz penal. Am ajuns aici cu niște panarame de miniștri”. Fostul președinte Traian Băsescu consideră că foștii miniștri ai Energiei și premierii care au decis închiderea unor capacități de producție fără să construiască altele noi sunt responsabili pentru actuala criză energetică. El cere instituirea stării de urgență și lansează un atac dur la adresa celor care au condus sectorul energetic, pe care îi numește „panarame” și „papițoi”.

Semnalizarea în sensul giratoriu: Greșeala pe care o fac mulți șoferi fără să știe. Explicațiile Poliției Române. Mulți șoferi folosesc semnalizarea atunci când intră într-un sens giratoriu, convinși că procedează corect. Poliția Română atrage însă atenția că această practică nu este prevăzută de Codul Rutier și poate crea confuzie în trafic. Autoritățile explică în ce situații este obligatorie folosirea semnalizării.

Criză energetică în Ungaria: centrala nucleară de la Paks mai produce doar 480MW, din 2000MW. Restricții la consumul de apă. Premierul ungar Peter Magyar a anunțat sâmbătă dimineață că principala centrală nucleară a țării, de la Paks, mai produce doar 480 de MW de energie, de aproape patru ori mai puțin decât capacitatea maximă, de 2.000 de MW. Aceasta centrală produce în mod normal jumătate din necesarul de energie al Ungariei. Din cauza valului de căldură, a fost impusă o restricție pentru apă, de nivel 1, în toată țara, și au intrat în vigoare reguli stricte. La Budapesta a fost doborât un record de căldură vechi de un secol, iar zilele următoare ar putea aduce noi maxime. Valul de căldură afectează deja funcționarea magazinelor: acestea își reduc consumul de energie electrică.

Migranții au trecut granița din Maroc în Spania după o mobilizare pe rețelele de socializare: noi informații despre criza din Ceuta. Noi informații despre ce i-a mânat pe migranți să ia cu asalt exclava spaniolă Ceută și să treacă granița dintre Maroc și Spania arată o mobilizare fără precedent pe rețelele sociale. 60 de mii de oameni au intrat în Ceuta, dar peste 53.000 dintre ei s-au intors deja în Maroc. Armata și forțele de ordine rămân mobilizate în exclava spaniolă până la rezolvarea totală a situației. Din păcate 57 de oameni au murit în apele mării, pentru că nu au reușit să ajungă la mal, în încercarea de a trece graniță maritimă, singura cale care le-ar fi dat șansa de a nu fi retrimiși imediat în țara de origine.

Succession : du changement dès ce 1er août Unsplash. A partir de ce samedi, le plafond net permettant de renoncer gratuitement à une succession est porté à 6.664,95 euros grâce à l’indexation, a indiqué vendredi la Fédération du notariat (Fednot). Jusqu’à présent, cette procédure gratuite devant un notaire était limitée aux successions d’une valeur maximale de 6.093,20 euros. L’an dernier, 57.742 personnes ont renoncé à une succession en Belgique. Parmi elles, 49.802 ont eu recours à la possibilité de le faire gratuitement auprès d’un notaire. Lorsqu’une personne est appelée à hériter, elle dispose de trois options : accepter la succession, y renoncer ou l’accepter sous bénéfice d’inventaire. En cas de renonciation, les créanciers du défunt ne peuvent plus réclamer le paiement des dettes à l’héritier. Celui-ci renonce toutefois également à l’ensemble des biens composant la succession et ne peut plus revendiquer les effets personnels du défunt. Les citoyens peuvent désormais accomplir gratuitement cette démarche auprès d’un notaire, alors qu’elle devait auparavant être effectuée devant le tribunal. « Nous constatons que la possibilité de renoncer gratuitement à une succession via un notaire est de mieux en mieux connue du grand public », a expliqué Carol Bohyn, notaire et porte-parole de Notaris.be. En théorie, un héritier dispose d’un délai de 30 ans pour renoncer à une succession. Carol Bohyn recommande toutefois de ne pas attendre trop longtemps. « Sinon, il existe un risque d’accomplir un acte qui sera considéré comme une acceptation tacite de la succession. Dans ce cas, il faudra malgré tout payer les dettes du défunt », a-t-elle averti. A titre d’exemple, le simple fait de transférer une petite somme du compte bancaire du défunt vers celui de l’héritier peut être interprété comme une acceptation tacite de la succession. À lire aussi Succession : anticiper l’avenir pour protéger ses proches Le plafond pour renoncer gratuitement à une succession est indexé dès ce samedi. Par Belga Le 1/08/2026 à 11:00

Castel : la bataille se poursuit entre Gregory Clerc et la fille du fondateur. Une décision de la justice à Singapour rendue ce 30 juillet relance le bras de fer au long cours entre le directeur général de Castel et une partie des héritiers du fondateur Pierre Castel.

Ethiopian Airlines : une croissance forte mais pas assez d’avions, le paradoxe du leader africain de l’aérien. Avec 9,1 milliards de dollars de revenus, Ethiopian Airlines signe sa meilleure année. Mais les coûts à la hausse, sa flotte sous tension et une marge nette africaine en forte chute nuancent ce résultat.

RDC-Rwanda : ce que l’on sait du projet controversé de démobilisation des FDLR. Le gouvernement congolais a présenté un protocole d’accord qui ouvre la voie à la dissolution du groupe fondé par d’anciens génocidaires hutu rwandais. Kinshasa y voit une avancée majeure, tandis que Kigali dénonce une manipulation.

Le premier Sénat du Bénin entre en fonction. Instaurée par la révision constitutionnelle de novembre 2025, la première Chambre haute du pays est composée de 25 parlementaires. Reste à désigner son siège et surtout, son président.

Cameroun : pourquoi les accusations du capitaine Effoudou contre Ferdinand Ngoh Ngoh créent le scandale. Déserteur et visé par un mandat d’arrêt pour escroquerie, l’ancien chef du bureau de renseignement de l’état-major de Paul Biya brise le silence depuis l’Europe. Ses accusations visant le secrétaire général de la présidence secouent Yaoundé.

Fintech : le régulateur de la Cemac en mission pour assainir le paiement électronique. Avec 3,74 milliards de transactions en 2024, le paiement mobile domine largement les échanges financiers en Afrique centrale. Le régulateur prépare un cadre inédit qui va remodeler le marché afin de mieux le contrôler.

Maroc-Espagne : afflux de migrants à Ceuta, neuf morts. Des centaines de personnes ont convergé dans la soirée du 30 juillet dans le nord du Maroc vers l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta. Plusieurs milliers de migrants y sont entrés ces derniers jours et neuf sont morts en tentant de la rejoindre à la nage.

À Pékin, les confidences des diplomates chinois sur le Maroc. Dix ans après la signature du partenariat stratégique entre les deux pays, Rabat continue d’occuper une place singulière dans la stratégie chinoise envers « le Sud global ».

Djibril Ouattara : « La Côte d’Ivoire s’inspire de l’Estonie pour développer ses infrastructures numériques publiques ». Le ministre ivoirien de la Transition numérique et de l’Innovation technologique veut porter la contribution de son secteur de 6 % à 15 % du PIB à l’horizon 2030. Et compte tout mettre en œuvre pour y parvenir. Entretien.

À l’ONU, un premier « vote indicatif » décevant pour Macky Sall. Si tout n’est pas encore joué, le premier scrutin secret visant à désigner le prochain secrétaire général de l’Organisation des Nations unies dessine une tendance défavorable aux deux candidats africains, dont Macky Sall.

Guerre au Soudan : les Boeing d’un contractant américain et l’étrange pont aérien vers les FSR. Une enquête de Reuters et un projet de rapport de l’ONU révèlent un pont aérien clandestin au profit des FSR d’Hemetti, qui aurait été opéré en partie depuis le Tchad. L’affaire ravive les soupçons sur le soutien des Émirats arabes unis aux paramilitaires soudanais.

Algérie-France : pourquoi Abdelmadjid Tebboune refuse toujours de parler à Emmanuel Macron. Deux ans après le soutien de Paris à la souveraineté marocaine sur le Sahara occidental, le président algérien n’a toujours pas pardonné à son ami français ce qu’il considère comme une trahison. Une rupture personnelle qui hypothèque l’ensemble de la relation franco-algérienne.

Afreximbank : les raisons de son retour au dollar. Après cinq ans d’émissions en yens et en yuans, la banque renoue avec le dollar en levant 1,5 milliard. Derrière ce grand retour se cachent une notation retrouvée et un pari calculé sur le calendrier.

Blocs pétroliers au Nigeria : la NNPC et Tony Elumelu recalés au profit de sociétés plus confidentielles. Le plus grand cycle d’octroi de licences du Nigeria depuis l’entrée en vigueur de la nouvelle loi pétrolière en 2021 a vu plusieurs producteurs pétroliers et gaziers établis repartir les mains vides.

Maroc : la crise au Moyen-Orient, point de bascule pour OCP ?. Le champion marocain des engrais sort d’une période de turbulences provoquée par le blocage du détroit d’Ormuz. Dans un décryptage vidéo, Jeune Afrique revient sur l’impact de cette épreuve pour le groupe et son patron, Mostafa Terrab.

Football en Côte d’Ivoire : l’accord secret qui a écarté Malick Tohé de la course à la tête de la FIF. Le vice-président de la « fédé » ivoirienne ne défiera pas son patron, Yacine Idriss Diallo. En échange, ce dernier lui a fait plusieurs concessions. Coulisses.

RDC : Katebe Katoto, frère de Katumbi et émissaire de Tshisekedi dans le Haut-Katanga. Alors que Félix Tshisekedi est en visite dans le Katanga, Raphaël Katebe Katoto y organise des consultations pour le compte du chef de l’État. Le demi-frère de l’opposant en exil Moïse Katumbi fait-il pour autant campagne pour le changement de Constitution voulu par le président ?

Affaire Zogo au Cameroun : ce qu’il faut retenir des déclarations du colonel Otoulou. L’audition de Jean-Pierre Otoulou, chef de la commission mixte ayant enquêté sur la mort de Martinez Zogo, se poursuit ces 3 et 4 août au tribunal militaire de Yaoundé. Jeune Afrique résume ses précédents passages à la barre.

Paul Biya toujours en Suisse, Ibrahim Traoré serre la vis, Fouzi Lekjaâ rebat les cartes… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer. Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique revient sur le séjour prolongé de Paul Biya en Suisse, analyse le durcissement de la politique religieuse d’Ibrahim Traoré au Burkina Faso, dresse le portrait du nouveau patron de Petrosen au Sénégal, décrypte le coup politique de Fouzi Lekjaâ au Maroc et s’interroge sur les critiques visant la Cour pénale internationale, accusée de cibler l’Afrique.

Ce discours de Hassan II que la Chine n’a jamais oublié. Une minute qui dure depuis des décennies. Alors que la Chine et le Maroc célèbrent les dix ans de leur « partenariat stratégique », le discours de 1960 de celui qui n’était encore que Moulay Hassan, à la tribune de l’ONU, continue d’éclairer les relations sino-marocaines.

Dangote peut-il remporter son pari de méga raffinerie au Kenya ?. Dangote ambitionne de faire du Kenya le pôle de raffinage de l’Afrique de l’Est avec un investissement de 17 milliards de dollars. Pour cela, il lui faut régler la question du financement, de l’approvisionnement et de la fiscalité… entre autres.

« C’est comme si j’étais prisonnier dans un paradis » : le Cap-Vert, refuge précaire pour de nombreux homosexuels africains persécutés. Etat d’Afrique le plus tolérant envers les LGBT+, d’après une enquête d’Afrobarometer, l’archipel accueille de nombreux Africains qui fuient la répression liée à leur orientation sexuelle. Mais l’absence de politique d’asile les empêche d’obtenir des titres de séjour.

Espagne : plus de 1 500 personnes sont arrivées en provenance du Maroc à Ceuta « ces derniers jours », annoncent les autorités régionales, qui évoquent une « urgence humanitaire absolue ». Des images, filmées par des chaînes de télévision locales, montrent des dizaines d’hommes et d’adolescents arriver à la nage sur les côtes de l’enclave espagnole. Jeudi soir, le gouvernement espagnol a annoncé le déploiement de l’armée « pour maintenir la sécurité dans la ville de Ceuta ».

Qui succédera à Antonio Guterres ? Les clés de la sélection du prochain secrétaire général de l’ONU. Sept personnes sont candidates au poste de plus haut fonctionnaire des Nations unies. Dans un paysage diplomatique fragmenté, le choix pourrait se révéler particulièrement difficile.

Comment l’unique récif corallien du Bénin a été redécouvert. Parti sur la trace d’une étude menée en 1963 et 1964, le chercheur Gérard Zinzindohoué est parvenu à localiser des coraux au large des côtes béninoises. Une découverte majeure, alors que le Cap-Vert était jusqu’à présent le seul pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest à contenir cet écosystème.

Comment l’uranium congolais transite vers la Chine sous les radars. Officiellement, la République démocratique du Congo ne produit pas d’uranium. Mais en vingt ans, 2 000 tonnes de ce minerai radioactif crucial pour l’industrie nucléaire auraient été exportées vers la Chine, selon une enquête de plusieurs journalistes et chercheurs partagée avec « Le Monde ».

Au Burkina Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré écarte le numéro deux de la junte. Mois après mois, le président burkinabé élimine tous ceux qui pourraient déstabiliser son régime. Dernier à en faire les frais, le capitaine Oumarou Yabré, considéré jusque-là comme le deuxième personnage de la junte au pouvoir à Ouagadougou.

Espagne : des centaines de personnes entrées illégalement dans l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta. De nombreuses images montrent des dizaines d’hommes et d’adolescents arriver à la nage, du Maroc voisin, sur les côtes de l’enclave espagnole.

Un afflux massif de migrants à Ceuta ravive les tensions entre l’Espagne et le Maroc. Des dizaines de milliers de personnes, des jeunes hommes et des adolescents dans leur immense majorité, ont soudainement rejoint par la mer, jeudi, depuis le Maroc, l’enclave espagnole située sur continent africain.

Au Sénégal, après les gays, les lesbiennes ciblées par une vague d’arrestations. Depuis l’adoption, mi-mars, d’une loi réprimant plus durement l’homosexualité, plus d’une centaine d’hommes ont été arrêtés. Mercredi 29 juillet, huit femmes ont à leur tour été interpellées. La répression s’élargit.

La RDC annonce avoir négocié la reddition des FDLR dans l’Est, point d’achoppement du processus de paix avec le Rwanda. En annonçant un protocole d’accord sur la reddition du groupe armé, Kinshasa veut mettre Kigali au pied du mur et montrer au médiateur américain que « les engagements pris sont respectés ».

« Pour répondre aux aspirations des Algériens, les pouvoirs publics doivent garantir un véritable pluralisme et renforcer les libertés publiques ». En Algérie, l’abstention lors des élections législatives du 2 juillet a été de 79 %. Dans une tribune au « Monde, l’homme politique algérien Zoheir Rouis souligne le risque d’une dépolitisation de plus en plus forte de la société.

Ceuta : plus de 60 000 migrants sont entrés par le Maroc, l’Espagne dénonce une « attaque » contre « son intégrité territoriale ». Le premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, s’est rendu sur place dans une ambiance électrique, ciblant des rumeurs lancées par des « mafias de trafiquants d’être humains » d’être à l’origine de cet afflux. Le président de l’enclave autonome, qui a rendu public ce chiffre, dit « qu’il est impossible d’absorber cette pression ».

A Ceuta, les images des dizaines de milliers d’exilés qui tentent de traverser la frontière espagnole. En photos | Les images prises sur place montrent les foules de personnes traversant la frontière à pied ou par la mer, les interventions des forces de l’ordre espagnoles ou marocaines.

Ebola : en RDC, plus de 3 500 cas recensés en quelques mois, plus que lors de l’épidémie la plus meurtrière de l’histoire du pays. Vendredi, 3 532 cas de la maladie à virus Ebola ont été confirmés dans cinq provinces du pays, selon les données publiées par les autorités congolaises. Parmi ces 3 532 cas, 1 556 personnes sont mortes.

Ceuta : l’Espagne dénonce une « attaque » contre « son intégrité territoriale ». Le premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, qui s’est rendu sur place dans une ambiance électrique, s’est attaqué à des rumeurs lancées par des « mafias de trafiquants d’êtres humains », les accusant d’être à l’origine de cet afflux.

Quand le gouvernement américain publie une carte fantaisiste de l’Afrique. Lors d’une conférence internationale sur le sida, au Brésil, fin juillet, le département d’Etat a présenté une carte de l’Afrique où la Côte d’Ivoire s’est retrouvée dans le sud du continent et le Nigeria enclavé dans le Sahara. Le Cameroun, quant à lui, est devenu un Etat fantôme.

Remis en liberté, le rappeur et cinéaste marocain Mehdi Black Wind espère retrouver son autre port d’attache, Marseille. Artiste touche-à-tout et engagé contre les inégalités dans son pays, le Maroc, Mehdi Black Wind, de son vrai nom El Mahdi Lyoubi, avait été arrêté le 10 juillet sur sa terre natale. Son interpellation avait suscité un vaste élan de mobilisation.

Mohammed VI célèbre son règne en pleine crise migratoire avec l’Espagne. Environ 50 000 personnes ont rejoint clandestinement l’enclave espagnole, jeudi. Un nombre record, alors que le roi du Maroc fête ses vingt-sept ans sur le trône.

« C’était la chance de notre vie » : après un exil de seulement quelques heures à Ceuta, des dizaines de milliers de jeunes regagnent le Maroc. Encouragées par des messages sur les réseaux sociaux, quelque 50 000 personnes ont rejoint illégalement l’enclave espagnole depuis jeudi 30 juillet, un afflux sans précédent. Mais la plupart d’entre elles ont déjà été contraintes de faire le chemin retour.

EN DIRECT, Ceuta : 67 migrants sont morts en tentant de rejoindre l’enclave à la nage, selon un nouveau bilan du gouvernement espagnol. La plupart des 50 000 migrants entrés illégalement dans l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta sont retournés au Maroc, et l’intégrité de l’espace Schengen est « absolument garantie », a affirmé le gouvernement espagnol. La France et l’Italie ont tout de même durci leurs contrôles frontaliers avec l’Espagne malgré les garanties formulées par Madrid.

Daily Telegraph columnist argues Saudi Arabia should join G7. DUBAI: Saudi Arabia should be invited to join the Group of Seven nations as the organization adapts to a changing global order, according to a column published in the Daily Telegraph by former UK prime ministerial representative to Saudi Arabia Ken Costa. Costa argued that while the G7 was created in the aftermath of the 1970s oil crisis, the world has changed dramatically since then, with new economic and geopolitical powers emerging. Despite those shifts, he said the group remains largely unchanged and no longer reflects the realities of global influence.

Australia says net migration down as far-right popularity surges. SYDNEY: Australia’s immigration levels fell last year, official data showed on Thursday, as its center-left government seeks to combat an ascendent far-right riding a wave of public discontent over soaring housing prices and cost of living. Net overseas migration added 301,000 people to Australia’s population of 28 million last year, Canberra’s Bureau of Statistics reported. Immigration minister Tony Burke said the figure was down nine percent from a year earlier and 45 percent lower than a post-Covid peak in 2023.

DUBAI: Robert Tsitaishvili is the head chef of Qartuli, a Georgian restaurant in Downtown Dubai, where his goal, he says, is “to reinterpret Georgian culinary heritage for a contemporary audience.” Tsitaishvili has more than 12 years of experience spanning hotels and restaurants across Georgia and internationally, with a background that includes pastry and confectionery.

Bird flu kills 13,000 seal pups on remote Australian island. SYDNEY: A pathogenic strain of bird flu killed more than 13,000 elephant seal pups after infecting a breeding colony on a sub-Antarctic volcanic island, Australian scientists said Thursday. Researchers found the remote Heard and McDonald Islands littered with seal carcasses when they arrived on a research expedition in October 2025. Genetic testing confirmed the contagious H5 bird flu strain had killed seals, penguins and birds living on the rocky outcrop — the first time it had been detected in one of Australia’s external territories.

Private schools in Sindh to decide weekly working days at their own convenience, education department says. All private schools in Sindh have been allowed to decide their weekly teaching and working days according to their own schedules and convenience, the Sindh Education and Literacy Department said on Friday. A circular issued by the province’s Directorate of Inspection and Registration of Private Institutions clarified a notification issued by the education department on July 29, which directed that classes would be held six days a week at schools and colleges across the province from August 1 until further notice. The new circular clarified that the directive would not apply to privately managed schools. “It is hereby clarified for all privately managed schools across the province of Sindh that they may manage their weekly working days according to their own schedules and operative convenience,” Additional Director (Registration) Rafia Javed said in the circular. A copy of the circular is available with Dawn . In its July 29 notification, seen by Dawn , the Education and Literacy Department said: “In supercession of this department’s notification of even number dated March 31, 2026, it is hereby notified that all public and private educational institutions under the administrative control of the School and Literacy Education Department, Government of Sindh, shall observe a six-day working week (Monday to Saturday) with effect from August 1, 2026 till further orders.” The College Education Department issued its own version of the notification a day later, directing that a six-day working week be observed by all public and private educational institutions under its administrative control. On March 31, as cited in the two notifications, the Sindh government had announced that Saturday and Sunday would be “off” days at educational institutions, as part of the austerity and fuel conservation measures adopted to deal with the economic impact of the US-Israeli war on Iran. The Sindh chief minister’s spokesperson, however, told Dawn that teachers had also stopped working on Saturdays, although the March decision applied only to students. He said this had affected students’ education and the completion of the annual curriculum. The six-day week was introduced to facilitate completion of the curriculum.

Supreme Court accepts PTI founder’s chamber appeal, orders fixation of case before bench. ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) on Friday accepted a chamber appeal moved by former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan and ordered early fixation of the case before an apex court bench as early as possible. Imran had filed a petition before the SC, requesting that he be shifted to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital and granted access to his family and personal physicians. Through the chamber appeal, Imran challenged the SC Registrar’s order that returned petitions seeking his transfer to Shifa International Hospital, Islamabad, as well as access to his personal physicians, family and counsel, and the provision of medical details to his family. The SC Registrar had returned the petition on the grounds that no signed power of attorney had been attached to the petition. On Friday, Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari appeared before the chamber of Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi to plead the case. Consequently, the objections earlier raised by the Registrar’s Office were removed after being declared null and void. The counsel was also directed to furnish a signed power of attorney, and the office was ordered to assign a case number to Khan’s petition. The SC also ordered that the petition moved by Dr Uzma Khan, the sister of Imran, be heard along with the case. The chamber appeal argued that the Registrar had exceeded his administrative authority, as the Registrar’s Office was primarily vested with administrative and procedural powers relating to the filing and processing of cases. It said determining maintainability, particularly where constitutional or statutory interpretation was involved, was a judicial function requiring legal reasoning and consideration of rival submissions. The petition also sought to convert the present petition into an appeal and direct that a medical examination of the petitioner be arranged by physicians of his choice, including Dr Khurram Mirza, Dr Asim Yusuf, Dr Faisal Sultan and Dr Samina Niazi, at the earliest. Moreover, the petition also sought the immediate transfer of the petitioner to Shifa International Hospital, Islamabad, for treatment and a comprehensive medical examination, along with continued access to his physicians, family members and counsel during his incarceration and treatment. Likewise, Dr Uzma had also challenged before the SC the Islamabad High Court’s ruling refusing to shift him to Shifa International Hospital, allow access to his personal physicians, family and counsel, and provide medical details to the family. The petition explained that Imran and his wife were currently incarcerated at Adiala jail, while his two sons lived abroad. As his sister and a doctor by qualification, the applicant had natural love and affection for her brother and was seriously concerned about his health and well-being, which, it alleged, were being jeopardised by the official acts and omissions of the respondents. It maintained that the appellant was Imran’s closest relative in Pakistan and therefore had the legal standing to file the appeal. Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January and receives government-provided treatment . The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations. The opposition has also demanded that the former premier be shifted to Shifa International Hospital, be treated in the presence of his personal physicians and allowed to meet his family.

Good governance 'quintessential' for security and stability of Pakistan: DG ISPR. Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Friday termed good governance “quintessential” for Pakistan’s security and stability. He made the remarks while addressing a press conference on the country’s overall security situation, particularly the situation in Balochistan. The DG ISPR, during his presser, commented on Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks about the need for new administrative units in Pakistan: “We have been saying this earlier also as a primary stakeholder in security that good governance is essential for the security and stability of Pakistan.” Without this, he stressed that none of Pakistan’s issues could be resolved. The military spokesperson said the National Action Plan (NAP), with its 14-point agenda and the consensus of all political parties, required good governance for its implementation, adding, “Good governance is quintessential for Pakistan.” “Now, how to achieve good governance? The politicians and political parties have to decide. If you ask us, yes, there has to be a serious discussion on it.” “Now our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,” the DG ISPR said, adding that it had to be done according to the will of the people of Pakistan. “The will of the people of Pakistan is superior. If good governance requires an administrative reset, then it has to be done through constitutional methods, legal procedures and political representatives.” 10 terrorists killed per day in 2026 At the outset of the briefing, the military spokesperson said 40,348 intelligence-based operations had been conducted this year so far, adding that the figure included operations carried out by all security forces, including police, civil armed forces, intelligence agencies and the armed forces. Of these operations, the majority were carried out in Balochistan, with the number exceeding 31,000, he said. The DG ISPR added that a total of 3,145 terrorism incidents had taken place in the country in 2026, of which 1,971 were reported from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 1,148 from Balochistan and 26 from other parts of the country. During this period, he continued, 2,084 confirmed terrorists were killed. “This comes to an average of 10 terrorists being killed every day, which is the highest ratio ever,” he added. Meanwhile, security forces were undertaking nearly 200 intelligence-based operations (IBOs) a day. “So these IBOs are going on every hour.” The DG ISPR further stated that “819 Pakistanis have been martyred” in incidents of terrorism during the ongoing year, which amounted to four a day. This comprised 303 army personnel, 194 law enforcers, including police and civil armed forces personnel, and 322 civilians. He added that 28 suicide bombing incidents had taken place this year, “the majority of which were carried out by Afghan nationals […] and people associated with their security forces”. Comparing the figures for terrorists killed last year and in 2026, he said 2,597 were killed in 2025 and 2,084 this year so far. Pointing out that five months were left before 2026 would end, he said, “The way the kinetic prong of the counter-terrorism is maturing, responding and delivering, that is before you.” He further elaborated that the number of martyrs in comparison to slain terrorists was higher, but the tide started turning in 2024. And in 2025, “for each martyr we were taking out minimum two [terrorists], and this year, we are taking out minimum 2.5 [terrorists].” Here, he added, a valid question to ask would be why terrorism incidents were rising. “Because once returns from other elements of their strategy begin diminishing, they focus more here. And you saw when their direct strategy during Marka-i-Haq failed, they started investing a lot more here,” he explained. The DG ISPR added that this also had to do with the “agenda of the terrorist-supporting Taliban regime” and the clarity demonstrated by the state of Pakistan. “These terrorists and their sponsors have come to understand that there is no space for appeasement or any talks with them […] They know that the state is telling them very clearly that either you submit to the state’s will in accordance with the law and the Constitution, or we are here and fighting,” he said. Moreover, he added, this also had to do with the proactive nature of the operations. “These [terrorism] incidents also rise because when we get proactive […] there will be more engagements.” ‘Hard state?’ Speaking of the “perception that the situation in Balochistan has worsened”, he said the matter would be examined through three questions. The first question was what the issue was, the second was what was happening and the third was what was being done, he said. Coming to the first question, he said the issue was not specific to Balochistan alone but related to the overall security environment in Pakistan. The issue, he said, was “Hard state, question mark”. “Are we a hard state? Unfortunately, not,” the military’s spokesperson added. Explaining the reason behind his answer, he said a hard state was one where the Constitution and the law applied equally to everyone. “That is what a hard state is. It does not mean a military-run state; it does not mean an armed forces-dominated state,” he added. The DG ISPR said a state where all matters were decided in accordance with the Constitution and the law, where everyone was equal, was a hard state. In such a state, there would be security and stability, and there would be no grievances. Then there was also the matter of obligations versus rights, he said, adding that it pertained to being aware of one’s responsibilities before speaking about one’s rights. “We are all taking up grievances — at some places slogans are also being raised in connection with those grievances and even arms are being taken up in some instances — and all those grievances [pertain to demands for rights],” he said. Saying that the demands for rights and the grievances may be genuine, he added that obligations needed to be fulfilled first. “Let me try to explain the context constitutionally,” he said, quoting Article 5 of the Constitution. The provision came before Article 8, which elaborated on fundamental rights, he said, adding that Article 5 stated: “Loyalty to the state and obedience to the Constitution and law. It says loyalty to the state is the basic duty of every citizen. Full stop. Absolutely clear.” “The second part of the provision states that obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be.” So the Constitution was “clear that we have some fundamental duties, including the need to be loyal to the state”. “If we are loyal to the state and we are obedient to the Constitution and the law, then you can talk about your rights,” he said. Citing a statement by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the National Workshop in Balochistan recently, he said when the rights movement is talked about, why not an “obligations movement”. “There has to be a movement for the obligation of every citizen,” he asserted. Further speaking of the obligations, he said, “Is this not an obligation for every citizen that our first and final identity should be Pakistani? … We are citizens of this state, so our first identity and our last identity and the foremost identity is being a Pakistani. “It is our obligation to acknowledge the fundamental position, the central position of the state of Pakistan because if there is the state, there is politics, there is life […] These are our fundamental obligations. “Are we working towards that? Let’s think about it.” Focusing on Balochistan, he said the fundamental issues in the province were elitism, sardarism and the desire to maintain the status quo. “This is that part of society which believes it has no obligations and only thinks of its rights. The elites and the sardars are a part of it. And I am not talking about all of them, but those who believe that this status quo must be maintained,” the DG ISPR said. He added that this status quo predated 1947, under which a poor man’s child could not get an education or progress in life. Those who did not want the status quo to change were the “prime movers of terrorism because they are afraid that the times are changing”. Then there was the issue of the desire for appeasement, the DG ISPR said. “They carry out terrorism, they talk about terrorism and say that Balochistan is getting out of hand. Then they expect that we talk to them and appease them […] No, we will not. We will talk with the actual stakeholders, who are the people of Balochistan,” he added. “You are not the stakeholder. You are only a stakeholder in your own and your family’s fortunes.” The military’s spokesperson went on to say that the problem with such elements was that they were not being appeased. “They have this habit of thinking that the Levies force is their private force, their sardari force.” “So once you start turning Balochistan’s Levies into a police force, they have a problem.” He further said that these elements were involved in smuggling in the name of business. “And if you stop this, there is terrorism. They promote terrorism and say Balochistan is getting out of hand.” Moving on, the DG ISPR said a third issue was “external power play”. The “elitists and sardarists have a common agenda”, he said, adding that “external powers” realised that Balochistan was blessed not only with “a very vibrant and very progressive human resource” but also with natural resources. “It has a blue economy, agriculture. They know the potential of Balochistan. They realise that when Balochistan rises, the whole of Pakistan rises and the region rises. And they have a problem, so they get physically involved through these terrorists […] and they find ready partners in these elitists and sardarists,” he said. Moreover, there was the issue of “contiguous support bases”, especially from Afghanistan. He said the business of the Afghan Taliban regime was terrorism and that, through terrorism, it sustained its economy, state and even diplomacy. “Even their diplomacy is centred on terrorism. What is common between India and Afghanistan, except their DNA? The only thing common is terrorism,” he added. “What is common between Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij ? Nothing. One is secular and nationalist, and the other is hardcore religious extremist. But because they are carrying out coordinated operations now…” he said. The government labelled the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan as Fitna-al-Khawarij and designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. He further stated that propaganda was another issue, which, he said, had three strands: a sense of deprivation, lack of representation and missing persons. Sharing data on facilities in various areas of Balochistan, he said the province’s per capita budget was more than Rs75,000, which was higher than that of any other province. “Then on what basis is this narrative of a sense of deprivation in Balochistan spun? It is spun on actions to prevent development. That is why they kill labourers and attack roads, hospitals and bridges. Are these military targets?” the DG ISPR questioned. Coming to the issue of lack of representation, he said same people and their families were in the assemblies since 1973. “Most of them are the same khanzaday and nawabzaday . It’s the same religious parties and same names, and either they win or their family members win. If they win, it is democracy, but if they don’t win, [the narrative is] there is dictatorship.” On missing persons, he said the government had formed a commission to inquire into the matter. The DG ISPR added the commission had received just 10,901 applications since its formation in the early 2010s. Of those, 9,372 cases had been disposed of, he said, adding that in 4,896 of the disposed-of cases, missing people had returned home, around 1,030 were located in prisons, 308 were found dead and 2,400 cases were declared as misreported cases. Moreover, he said, 2,933 of the total cases were reported from Balochistan, among which 2, 767 had been disposed of. He went on to say persons reported missing in the remaining cases were often found among killed terrorists after operations. The DG ISPR added that terrorists were now also filming attacks to build a narrative that the situation in Balochistan was deteriorating. He further pointed out that Balochistan’s area was 347,190 sq km, which was more than the area of many countries, as he elaborated on the need for more security personnel. He said this while speaking about raising a new command of the Frontier Corps, FC West, and its attached units in the province. Sharing details of the current situation in Balochistan, he said terrorists had killed 178 civilians in the province this year, kidnapped 55 civilians, damaged roads and bridges at 24 places, set property on fire at 60 places and there were 47 incidents of looting. Police and Levies were targeted in 105 incidents, he said. They carry out terrorist activities, film it and release videos, and “elitists and sardarists start crying over the deteriorating situation”, he added. They target infrastructure and run this propaganda about a lack of development, the military’s spokesperson said, mentioning Indian involvement in such activities as well. Here, he also spoke about the challenges faced by police as first responders, again citing Balochistan’s vast area as well as capacity constraints. The DG ISPR further said that previous governments that let Levies be a “sardari force” were answerable in this regard. He questioned why the funds were not translated into equipment for police, adding, “Because you did not want to respond to your BLA pets.” He then lauded police for fighting against terrorism, asking why were they not being acknowledged. “Because terrorists are making videos […] that are used to create a narrative,” he answered. Moreover, he said terrorists were “honey-trapping” girls. They would kidnap and abuse them and then blackmail them into committing acts of terrorism. He also said that 300 Indian websites were being operated for terrorism-related activities in Balochistan, more than 1,000 social media accounts were being used for the purpose and that a “hostile diaspora” was also involved in propaganda related to terrorism. Explaining the social media ecosystem used by terrorists, the DG ISPR said: “First, an event or incident is seeded, right or wrong, and then it is framed by initiators, who hand it over to amplifiers. Then mass amplification is done by mainstream Indian media, channels and their print media as well, from where it is picked up by international media, and then you take it and run it as facts.” Citing the example of the July 16 attack on a convoy in Mastung, the military spokesperson said that accounts associated with BYC, BLA and political parties based abroad were involved in amplifying it. He further noted: “There is already an ecosystem here that whenever there is negative news about Pakistan, certain actors are always there to mark their attendance.” Speaking of kinetic operations against terrorists in Balochistan, he said currently security forces were conducting Operation Shaban , which had been morphed into Operation Al-Azm. He also said that most of the operations were carried out jointly by the army, FC and police. Moreover, Operation Ghazab lil-Haq was also under way against the Afghan Taliban. The military’s spokesperson said that 2.6 million Afghans had been repatriated to Afghanistan from Pakistan, of whom 600,000 were repatriated this year. The general also said that work was underway to strengthen the capacity of security forces in the province, including the establishment of FC West in Chagai, which he said would ensure the “security of the mineral corridor”. The DG ISPR added that the government was working on strengthening the police force as well, including the posting of newly recruited ASPs to Balochistan and the provision of bulletproof vehicles, among other measures. He also stressed the significance of “empowering and appeasing” the common people of Balochistan. “We are committed to engaging and talking directly with people,” he said. He added that Rs70 billion had been allocated to socioeconomic projects in Balochistan and Rs24bn for the Balochistan Special Development Initiative. He further stated that development projects aimed at improving road connectivity, IT training and human resources were also in progress. Concluding his address, the DG ISPR played a video of the government’s direct engagements with people in Balochistan. “This is the bright future of Balochistan that we need to further nurture, develop and propagate because Balochistan has a remarkable future,” he said. “In the words of the Field Marshal, and he says it with a lot of conviction, within 5-10 years it is going to be the richest province; it is going to be a game changer. And the bigger the potential, the bigger the threats we face, but we, the people of Pakistan and Balochistan, will overcome [them].” ‘Kashmir jugular vein of Pakistan’ On the unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), DG ISPR held, “Kashmir was, is and will remain a jugular vein of Pakistan.” “Only one voice is coming from Pakistan: Kashmir will be Pakistan, and there is only one voice coming from Kashmir: Pakistan is ours, we are Pakistani, nothing can change that.” Referring to the Joint Awami Action Committee’s (JAAC) protests, he said: “We knew who was behind that movement, but we wanted them to expose themselves. They have been exposed now.” He said the JAAC opposed refugee representation in AJK’s legislature; however, the state had “wholeheartedly” asked them to contest the elections and approach the matter through legal and constitutional means. “However, they want to pursue this by force, but only the state has the monopoly of violence.”

Shangla mourns 28 miners killed in Balochistan coal mine accident. SHANGLA: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Shangla district is mourning the deaths of 28 young coal miners, including 23 residents of Mian Kaly, who were killed in a gas explosion at a coal mine on the outskirts of Quetta on Thursday. The Shangla Coal Mine Workers Association said that following the deaths of 23 miners from Mian Kaly, almost every household in the village was mourning the loss of a family member. Abid Yaar, president of the Shangla Coal Mine Workers Association, said that Mian Kaly had become the epicentre of repeated coal mine tragedies. “A total of 28 deceased workers were from Shangla district — 23 from Mian Kaly (Pir Abad), two from Kana, and one each from Bada and Gata Bely Baba,” he said. He added that the victims, aged between 17 and 25, belonged to the same families and were cousins or close relatives. According to Yaar, several of the deceased were orphans whose fathers had also lost their lives in previous coal mine accidents. He alleged that the tragedy resulted from the mine administration’s negligence and the absence of essential safety measures, claiming that there was no proper ventilation system in the government-run mine, which led to the deadly gas explosion. “It is not just an accident but a lifelong trauma for the families, orphans, widows and mothers who lost their loved ones. These young men had gone there only to earn a livelihood and support their families back home,” Yaar said. Responding to a question, he noted that Shangla lacked factories and other opportunities for skilled employment, forcing young people to work in hazardous coal mines and risk their lives to make ends meet. The victims’ family members criticised the government for not arranging ambulances to transport their loved ones’ bodies, adding that they had to bring the remains in a van at their own expense. According to the Shangla administration, one body arrived on Friday evening, with the others expected to arrive later at night and early on Saturday morning. Three of the miners who lost their lives in the tragedy were brothers. Earlier today, rescue teams recovered 32 bodies overnight from two coal mines in the Sorange coalfield near Quetta after a methane gas explosion, while the search for two more miners was underway. The explosion occurred on Thursday at a private coal mine in the Sorange coalfield, about 30 kilometres northeast of Quetta. The methane gas explosion triggered a fire, caused the mine to collapse, and affected another nearby mine. Chief Inspector of Mines Balochistan Muhammad Atif told Dawn that 34 miners were inside the two mines when the explosion occurred. “So far, 32 bodies have been recovered from both mines,” he said. “The operation is continuing in the mine where the explosion took place to recover two miners.” The explosion severely affected another mine near the main site, with 12 miners working in the second mine at the time. In June, at least three people were injured after explosive material used in mining accidentally detonated in the Khanuzai area. In April, at least five coal miners were killed in two separate mine accidents that took place in the Bolan and Duki coalfield areas of Balochistan.

Schools in Sindh to remain closed on August 4: education department. The Sindh government’s School Education and Literacy Department on Friday announced that schools in the province would remain closed on Aug 4 (Tuesday) in observance of Chehlum of Imam Hussain (AS). A notification available with Dawn states that all public and private educational institutions under the department “shall remain closed on Aug 4, 2026 (Tuesday) on account of Chehlum (20th Safar 1448 AH)”. The notification has been sent to the principal secretaries of the Sindh governor and chief minister, as well as other senior officials. The Chehlum of Imam Hussain is observed on Safar 20, highlighting the sacrifices rendered by Imam Husain (AS) and his companions in Karbala. Earlier today, the department said private schools in Sindh have been allowed to decide their weekly teaching and working days according to their own schedules and convenience. A circular issued by the province’s Directorate of Inspection and Registration of Private Institutions clarified a notification issued by the education department on July 29, which directed that classes would be held six days a week at schools and colleges across the province from August 1 until further notice. The new circular clarified that the directive would not apply to privately managed schools.

Pakistan welcomes Board of Peace developments under Gaza Peace Plan: PM Shehbaz. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that Pakistan welcomed developments under the Board of Peace towards implementing the disarmament process under the Gaza Peace Plan. Earlier today, US President Donald Trump said talks in Cairo between mediators and Hamas leaders on Thursday have led to a phased disarmament agreement in Gaza, but a Hamas official described the deal as a draft and US officials said Israel was sceptical the Palestinian group would surrender its weapons. “Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza,” Trump said in a social media post, adding that the disarmament would come in phases. In a social media post on X, PM Shehbaz said, “Pakistan welcomes developments under the Board of Peace towards the implementation of the disarmament process under the Gaza Peace Plan.” He emphasised that the mediating countries, including the United States of America, Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye, deserved “special appreciation for their efforts in achieving this progress”. Commending President Trump’s “courageous leadership”, the premier said that this represented “a significant achievement for the Board of Peace”. “Pakistan expresses the hope that with these developments, concrete steps will be taken towards implementing all commitments under the Gaza Peace Plan. He concluded by expressing hope that these efforts would lead to the realisation of the right to self-determination of the Palestinian people through a credible and time-bound political process, in line with international legitimacy and relevant UN resolutions. The prime minister added that this should result in the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. The board was initially proposed in September 2025 and formally established in January. Under its charter, the US government serves as its official depository and Trump has designated the Donald J Trump Institute of Peace in Washington as the Board’s headquarters. A UN Security Council resolution adopted in mid-November last year authorised the board, along with cooperating states, to establish an international stabilisation force in Gaza following a ceasefire that began in October under a Trump-backed plan accepted by Israel and Hamas. Pakistan is among the 14 countries that signed the charter of the Board of Peace on January 22 on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos, becoming a founding member of the body. The list of founding members also includes Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Albania, Bahrain, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cambodia, El Salvador, Egypt, Hungary, Indonesia, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kuwait, Mongolia, Morocco, Paraguay, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, the United Arab Emirates, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam, spanning the Middle East, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caucasus. The board was originally conceived to oversee the ceasefire and reconstruction of Gaza, but its charter expands its mandate to peace-building in all areas affected by or at risk of conflict.

Italy suspends Schengen agreement with Spain: foreign minister. Italy has suspended its Schengen agreement with Spain, Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Friday, calling the measure “unavoidable”. “The temporary suspension of Schengen with Spain is a necessary choice to safeguard the security of our citizens and defend the European borders,” he wrote in a post on X. He noted that the influx of migrants in Ceuta, Spain, “reminds us that the management of the Union’s borders is a shared responsibility among our countries, one toward the other”. “We must work together to prevent uncontrolled migrant flows from entering EU territory, with all the consequent risks and the threat of terrorism, which must be countered without hesitation,” he added. US President Donald Trump led far-right attempts on Friday on both sides of the Atlantic to make political capital from Spain’s migration crisis, portraying the migrant surge in Ceuta as a warning for America if his opponents get into power. “It’s terrible. Remember that picture. That’s going to be us in three years if the wrong side gets in,” Trump was quoted as saying by Fox News . “If the Democrats get in, you will not live a very good life.” With polls showing Trump’s support has fallen into the low 30 per cent range and opposition Democrats hoping to win at least partial control of Congress in November midterm elections, the crisis in Spain offers Republicans a chance to return to one of their political strongpoints. News footage of migrants overwhelming barriers to get into Ceuta — a tiny Spanish territory on the Moroccan coast — aired repeatedly on Fox News and went viral across right-wing Trump-allied social media accounts. In Europe, far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) co-leader Alice Weidel claimed in an X post that “Ceuta was left in ruins overnight” by the mass influx from Morocco. She argued that Germany is “likely the destination for most of these migrants”. “Germany must prepare itself: borders must be secured and rejections rigorously enforced,” wrote Weidel, whose party is backed by top Trump officials. Both Italy’s right-wing prime minister Giorgia Meloni and the populist right-wing ruling coalition in Finland called for excluding Spain from the European visa-free zone as a result of the situation. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis, a billionaire Trump supporter, said the Ceuta situation was caused by Spain’s policy of offering hundreds of thousands of migrants already in the country a legal status. “They are replacing Spaniards with migrants,” Babis said. ‘Invasion of the West’ Trump’s election victory over Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024 was fueled by voter worries over uncontrolled migration on the US-Mexico border and his lurid warnings of migrants coming to murder Americans and even to eat their pets. Trump’s vice president, JD Vance, posted news footage on Friday of migrants pouring into Ceuta on X and wrote it highlighted “radical left-wing globalist policies that have enabled the Invasion of the West.” “These images out of Spain are an unfortunate reminder of the consequences of mass migration,” Vance posted on X. Late on Thursday, White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, a chief architect of Trump’s anti-migration crackdown, posted video of the Ceuta crisis and said, “Democrats will see your home trampled and stolen by invaders and they will rejoice.”

Search operation for climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche suspended due to bad weather. GILGIT: The search and rescue operation for foreign climbers missing after an avalanche at Broad Peak was suspended late Friday due to adverse weather conditions in the region. Three bodies of missing climbers — one each from the United States, Nepal and Oman — were airlifted from Broad Peak to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters. Drone footage also indicated the presence of more climbers during the search operation. Earlier reports had said that four bodies were recovered; however, the toll was later revised down to three. Seven climbers remain missing. According to a press release issued by the Commissioner Baltistan Division, the search and rescue operation was launched following a formal request from tour operators. A three-member civil rescue team, led by renowned mountaineer Sarbaz Khan, was airlifted to Broad Peak Base Camp by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters. The team recovered the bodies of three climbers, identified as Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung and Mallory Geis from the United States. The bodies were later shifted to CMH Skardu by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters. The press release said the rescue operation had been temporarily suspended due to poor weather conditions and would resume on Saturday once conditions improved. Other Sherpas involved in mountaineering expeditions at the peak would also assist in the operation. The rescue team said signs indicating the presence of more climbers had also been spotted through drone footage. Despite the challenging terrain and harsh weather conditions at such high altitudes, the search operation was continuing with the cooperation of the Pakistan Army, local expert mountaineers and rescue teams. The Gilgit-Baltistan government expressed condolences to the families of the deceased climbers and assured them that all possible assistance would be provided in the rescue operation and the repatriation of the bodies to their respective countries. Experts said the chances of survival for the missing climbers were diminishing with each passing hour. Earlier, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said that the 10-member team included six Nepalese climbers, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American and a climber from China. The climbers from Nepal were identified as renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, Pur Bahadur Gurung, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa. It identified the remaining climbers as Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Wang Zhong from China and Mallory Geis from the United States. Rescue operation In a statement issued earlier in the day, ACP Senior Vice President Karrar Haidri said two Pakistan Army Aviation rescue helicopters, carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment, had been dispatched to support the ongoing search and rescue operation. The statement said the ACP president, along with the club’s senior leadership, remained in constant contact with the highest government authorities and relevant agencies to facilitate the rescue operation. “Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” it added. The club said it was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with all relevant stakeholders while expressing solidarity with the climbers’ families and the international mountaineering community. ACP’s General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that several expedition teams had jointly begun their summit push before the incident. He said GPS locations received from some of the missing climbers indicated that the avalanche had swept the group about 1,000 metres downhill, leaving them trapped. Shigri said there were also fears that some local high-altitude porters might have been affected by the avalanche. “We pray for the safety of all the climbers. It is a big incident,” he said. Meanwhile, Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Advocate directed all relevant departments to remain on high alert and expedite the search and rescue operation in coordination with the Pakistan Army, according to an official statement. He instructed the district administration and concerned authorities to utilise all available resources to ensure the climbers’ safety. Gilgit-Baltistan Minister for Tourism, Sports and Culture Naiknam Karim also expressed sorrow over the incident and said the provincial government was making every possible effort to locate and safely rescue the missing climbers. In a statement, he said “all relevant departments are in constant coordination and that every available resource was being utilised to support the ongoing search and rescue operation”. Expressing hope that the missing climbers would be found safe, the minister directed the concerned authorities to further expedite the rescue operation and ensure that all necessary logistical and operational support was provided to the teams working in the field. Purja, 43, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the elite Special Boat Service (SBS), has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide. He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 — then a record. In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 along with a team of nine other Nepalese climbers. Separately, in a post on X, the UK Embassy in Pakistan expressed concern at the incident. Seemingly referencing Purja, it also took note of a British-Nepali national missing in the expedition. “We are concerned by reports that several climbers have gone missing during a Broad Peak expedition, including a British-Nepali national,” the embassy said, adding that it remained in contact with Pakistani authorities. Sakhi, who hails from Hunza, had successfully summited Kanchenjunga (8,58­6m), the world’s 3rd highest mountain, in Nepal earlier in May. He had previously scaled K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I and Gasherbrum II without supplemental oxygen, establishing himself among the country’s strongest high-altitude climbers. Additional input from AFP

RLNG prices rocket to highest level in a decade. • LPG rates for August increased to Rs254.32 per kg • Ogra says five spot cargoes had to be procured after no shipment secured from Qatar • Regulator finally reveals lower prescribed prices for gas utilities, finalised on June 23 • Rs50bn savings from lower gas rates to be used for circular debt adjustment ISLAMABAD: In a major price shock, Ogra on Friday notified a record 32pc increase in regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) prices for August, fixing the rate at $25.83 per mmBtu for Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and $25.09 per mmBtu for Sui Southern Gas Company Limi­ted (SSGCL), while denying consumers about Rs50bn in savings from lower natural gas rates. This translates into a retail price of around Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The revised price is based on five imported LNG cargoes procured from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar due to the US war on Iran. This is the biggest-ever increase in RLNG prices in the commodity’s decade-long history. The latest increase comes on top of around a 15pc rise in RLNG prices last month, when the rate was fixed at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL. Compared with the February price of $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu, the RLNG rate for August is around 148pc higher. The sharp increase is expected to significantly raise fuel costs for power generation. The impact is already visible, as the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation rose to Rs31 per unit in May, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April. Meanwhile, Ogra also notified a 5.4pc (Rs12.89 per kg) increase in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices for August. It fixed the LPG price at Rs254.32 per kg with effect from Aug 1, compared with Rs241.43 per kg in July. In a belated disclosure, Ogra has revealed that it red­uced the prescribed prices for gas utilities by Rs134 per unit (7.4 per cent), resulting in savings of around Rs50 billion that will be used for circular debt adjustments instead of providing relief to consumers through lower gas prices. For the first time, the regulator did not upload its prescribed price determination, finalised on June 23 and shared with the government, on its website. Since its inception two decades ago, Ogra has publicly released its determinations while simultaneously sharing them with the government. In many cases, it also holds press briefings on its prescribed price determinations and the revenue requirements of gas utilities. However, it remained silent on queries for over a month and finally uploaded the determinations on its website this week after some interveners at public hearings raised concerns. The government has also maintained silence on the matter, although it has already informed the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that consumer-end gas prices would remain unchanged. The savings resulting from lower revenue requirements determined by the regulator for SNGPL and SSGCL would be used to reduce gas sector circular debt, which was last reported at around Rs3.5 trillion, a senior government official confirmed. As a result, Ogra has yet to notify consumer-end gas rates for the current fiscal year, which are required under the law and the IMF programme to take effect from July 1 every year. The fresh determinations would allow annual revenue of around Rs817 billion to the two gas utilities during the current fiscal year, including Rs501 billion for SNGPL and Rs315.8bn for SSGCL. The determinations showed that the prescribed gas price for SNGPL’s revenue requirement was reduced by Rs134 per mmBtu to Rs1,719 for FY2026-27 from Rs1,853 per mmBtu in FY2025-26, resulting in an annual revenue surplus of around Rs46.3bn. “In exercise of its power under section 8(1) of the Ordinance, the Authority, after taking into consideration points raised by interveners, clarifications provided by the petitioner, scrutiny of the petition and available record, provisionally determines the surplus in estimated revenue requirement for the said year at Rs46.279bn,” Ogra stated. It added that the surplus amount would be adjusted against previous years’ shortfall in accordance with the Federal Cabinet’s decision of June 30, 2024, which directed that prior-year shortfalls be adjusted to the extent possible during the current financial year. Accordingly, the regulator determined SNGPL’s estimated revenue requirement, net of revenues, at Rs501.110bn (Rs1,718.96 per mmBtu) for the current fiscal year. Similarly, the prescribed price for SSGCL’s revenue requirement for FY2026-27 was reduced by Rs86 per mmBtu, resulting in savings of Rs2.5bn. Ogra said it had provisionally determined a surplus of Rs1.421bn in estimated revenue requirement for the year. The regulator noted that, based on the currently notified prescribed price, an additional recovery of Rs1.073bn was available, leaving Rs2.494bn for adjustment of previous years’ shortfalls in line with the federal cabinet’s June 30, 2024 decision. Under the decision, the cabinet had directed Ogra to adjust previous years’ shortfalls to the extent of possible surplus during the current financial year. Accordingly, SSGCL’s revenue requirement, net of other revenues, was provisionally determined at Rs315.773bn (Rs1,691.24 per mmBtu) for the current fiscal year, compared with its previous rate of Rs1,777 per unit before June 30, 2026. It may be noted that SSGCL had sought an estimated revenue requirement of Rs1.274 trillion, including Rs545.28bn in unrecovered shortfalls from previous years. Karachi-based SSGCL supplies gas to consumers in Sindh and Balochistan, while Lahore-based SNGPL provides gas to consumers in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

Naqvi’s remarks ignite fresh debate in political circles. ISLAMABAD / HYDERABAD / LAHORE: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structur e and the carving out of new administrative units has ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation. Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad on Thursday, Mr Naqvi said the present system of governance had collapsed and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems. He urged all political parties to sit together and settle every outstanding issue, including the creation of new units and provinces, warning that without structural change the same debates would be taking place a decade from now. He described more administrative units as the only way to bring facilities closer to citizens, said new leadership was needed, and argued that the country’s youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops. PPP refers matter to CEC The PPP’s Central Executive Com­mittee will take up the question of new administrative units, party secretary general Nayyar Bokhari told Dawn , while insisting that the route must be constitutional rather than executive. Bokhari said the Constitution laid down a complete procedure, and that neither new provinces nor any change in provincial boundaries was possible without a two-thirds majority in the relevant provincial assembly, the National Assembly and the Senate. New provinces, he stressed, could not be brought about through an executive order. He said that if there was genuine seriousness about creating new provinces — South Punjab included — the matter should go to parliament and the constitutional requirements should be met. Mr Bokhari called on Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, whose party governs Punjab and the Centre, to begin the process in his own province, recalling that a resolution for a South Punjab province was already pending before the Punjab Assembly. Federal ministers, he said, should raise the issue in the cabinet and, once it was approved, Prime Minister Sheh­baz Sharif should consult PPP Chair­man Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on what he called an important national issue. The CEC would then deliberate, with every decision taken in line with the Constitution, democracy and the will of the people. Responding directly to the interior minister, Mr Bokhari said the proper forum for addressing flaws in the system was parliament rather than the me­dia, and asked who should be held responsible if the system was not working. ‘Sindh will not accept it’ Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah dismissed the proposal as a stereotype that the people of his province would never accept. Speaking briefly to journalists at Bhit Shah on Friday, the chief minister said he had seen the minister’s remarks about the system having collapsed, but was unclear on what exactly Mr Naqvi was referring to. He noted that Shehbaz Sharif was prime minister, that the PML-N governed Punjab, the PPP governed Sindh, a coalition ran Balochistan and the PTI controlled Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “If he thinks that this system is beyond repair now then he should come up with some proposals,” Mr Shah said. The minister had offered several suggestions, he added, but this particular one — new administrative units or provinces — was “a stereotype which people of this mystic land will not accept”. ‘Unconstitutional’ The Lahore High Court Bar Assoc­ia­tion condemned the interior minister’s statement on changing the governance system, calling it unconstitutional. In a joint statement, LHCBA Presi­dent Babar Murtaza, Vice President So­­­h­ail Qaiser Tarar and Finance Sec­retary Malik Ali Raza Khokhar said those responsible for the destruction of the existing order were now proposing a “new system”. The country’s progr­ess, survival and prosperity, they said, depended solely on strict adherence to the Constitution, the rule of law and complete independence of the judiciary. They criticised the minister for in­­v­i­ting politicians to alter the governance system at a time when, they claimed, popular political leaders and workers had been jailed for prolonged periods on fabricated and baseless charges. The office-bearers demanded the im­­mediate release of all detained political workers and said state institutions and agencies must end their intervention so that constitutional supremacy and judicial freedom could be guaranteed. Call for Naqvi’s resignation Awami Tehreek leaders accused the interior minister of advocating the division of Sindh under the cover of creating new provinces, and demanded that he step down. In a joint statement on Friday, party president Vasand Thari, secretary general Sajid Hussain Mahesar and other leaders said Mr Naqvi enjoyed the PPP’s backing and had, after the MQM and some media organisations, taken up the role of an undeclared spokesperson for the establishment in promoting the new provinces agenda. They said he had lost the moral and political justification to remain interior minister. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026
