HERO Foundation board reaffirms long-term commitment to military orphans at 2026 annual board meeting. The HERO Foundation Inc. held its Annual Board Meeting on July 23, 2026, led by Chairman Fernando Zobel de Ayala and attended by the Foundation's distinguished Board of Trustees. The meeting reaffirmed the Board's unwavering commitment to expanding educational opportunities for military orphans and ensuring the long-term sustainability of the Foundation During the meeting, the Board of Trustees—composed of the country's most respected business leaders—strengthened its commitment to HERO Foundation by endorsing long-term funding strategies and sustainability initiatives. These efforts aim to secure continuous educational support for the children of soldiers who were killed or permanently incapacitated in the line of duty, while advancing the Foundation toward greater financial self-sufficiency. "Our impact is vividly reflected in our numbers. For 2025-2026 school year, we supported 232 scholars from elementary school through college, with largest portion -46%- residing in Mindanao," said President Gen Emmanuel T Baustista AFP (Ret). "Each graduate overcame immense adversity with resilience and determination. They are living proof of what happens when a community unites behind a cause. Their success is not just a personal victory, but a testament to the transformative power of education.” Since its establishment in 1988, HERO Foundation has supported 2,777 military orphans, with 1,292 scholars successfully earning their college degrees. For School Year 2026–2027, the Foundation will provide educational assistance to 226 military orphan scholars, continuing its legacy of transforming lives through access to quality education. The Annual Board Meeting also highlighted the Foundation's ongoing efforts to strengthen partnerships with the private sector, government agencies, and individual donors, ensuring that the legacy of the nation's fallen heroes lives on through the education and success of their children. As HERO Foundation continues to grow, it remains committed to its mission of empowering military orphan scholars, creating opportunities for brighter futures, and honoring the enduring sacrifices of the country's brave servicemen and women.

The only address of its kind: The Residences at Terrazas de Punta Fuego. Luxury is often defined by location. True luxury, however, is defined by what endures: heritage, craftsmanship, and timeless design. For more than 275 years, Villeroy and Boch has shaped some of the world´s most distinguished homes, hotels, and residences through uncompromising German craftsmanship, timeless design, and enduring quality. By selecting the renowned European brand for The Residences at Terrazas de Punta Fuego, Landco Pacific reinforces its vision of creating homes that combine international standards of luxury with the natural beauty of Philippine coastal living. Through a partnership facilitated by Kuysen Enterprises, every residence will feature Villeroy and Boch, marking The Residences at Terrazas de Punta Fuego as one of the most comprehensive integrations of the brand across a single Philippine residential address. Rather than simply overlooking the sea, The Residences is conceived as a collection of homes built to European standards of luxury, where every detail is thoughtfully curated, every material chosen for longevity, and every space designed to enrich everyday living. "We are deeply honored to partner directly with Villeroy and Boch in bringing their craftsmanship to a celebrated Philippine residential address," said Erickson Y. Manzano, president and CEO of Landco Pacific Corporation. "More than introducing a globally respected European luxury brand to the country, this partnership reflects our vision of creating homes that marry the timeless elegance of European craftsmanship with the extraordinary beauty of Philippine coastal living." The collaboration began in Mettlach, Germany, where the Landco Pacific team met with Villeroy and Boch to discuss a shared vision for bringing authentic European craftsmanship to a Philippine residential address. It was a partnership founded on shared values: an unwavering commitment to quality, longevity, and design excellence. Today, Villeroy and Boch is an integral part of The Residences' broader vision. The brand's heritage and expertise complement a development conceived around thoughtful design, exceptional quality, and a lifestyle centered on comfort, wellbeing, and lasting value. That philosophy extends beyond bathrooms or fixtures. It defines the entire vision of The Residences. Inspired by the timeless appeal of Europe's most celebrated seaside communities, the development embraces architecture that maximizes natural light, sea breezes, and panoramic views while integrating thoughtfully designed wellness spaces, resort-style amenities, and generous outdoor living areas. Every residence is designed to encourage a slower, more intentional way of life, where luxury is experienced through comfort, craftsmanship, and an enduring connection with nature. The result is a rare union of two worlds: the sophistication and refinement of European luxury living set against the breathtaking coastline of Punta Fuego. It is a place where residents enjoy the warmth and beauty of the Philippine tropics without compromising the standards of design, quality, and craftsmanship associated with Europe's most iconic brands. More than an exclusive collaboration, the partnership with Villeroy and Boch reinforces the vision behind The Residences, to become the country's benchmark for internationally inspired beachfront living, where globally celebrated heritage brands find a natural home alongside one of the Philippines' most extraordinary coastal destinations. At The Residences, European luxury does not replace the beauty of the Philippines; it elevates it. A coastal legacy address The Residences represents one of the last opportunities to own a luxury beachfront home within the highly coveted Punta Fuego community in Nasugbu, Batangas, just two to three hours from Metro Manila, yet worlds away from city life. Conceived in the 1990s as the country's pioneering marina-front enclave, Punta Fuego's vision culminates here in a low-density development offering one- to three-bedroom residences, each with unobstructed sea views. To learn more about The Residences, visit https://theresidencespuntafuego.landco.ph/.

Tea for Harmony showcases Chinese tea culture in the Philippines. The rich traditions of Chinese tea culture took center stage at the Tea for Harmony Yaji Cultural Salon, bringing together diplomats, cultural leaders, and members of the media for an afternoon of tea appreciation and cross-cultural exchange. Hosted by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism of the People's Republic of China and the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Philippines, the event last July 29 highlighted the history, artistry, and enduring significance of tea in Chinese culture. Among those in attendance were Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino, alongside members of the diplomatic corps, dignitaries, and media representatives. Guests were introduced to Song Dynasty whisked tea, also known as Song-style diancha, a centuries-old preparation method in which finely ground tea is whisked into a delicate froth. The program also featured Tea Baixi, a traditional tea painting technique that uses tea foam as a canvas for intricate designs. Beyond the demonstrations, attendees learned about the evolution of Chinese tea-drinking traditions and the country's UNESCO-recognized traditional tea-making techniques and associated social practices. The cultural salon emphasized tea's role beyond the teacup, highlighting how the tradition continues to foster cultural exchange, mutual understanding, and friendship between China and the Philippines. Through demonstrations and discussions, the event offered guests an opportunity to experience one of China's enduring cultural traditions while reinforcing the value of shared heritage and people-to-people connections.

Centeno, Amit hurdle openers, forge early duel in world 10-ball. Defending champion Chezka Centeno and Rubilen Amit hurdled their respective opening-round assignments to set up an early blockbuster showdown in the 2026 WPA Women’s 10-Ball Championship in Rome, Italy on Friday, July 31. Fresh from capturing the world 8-ball crown just days earlier, Centeno bounced back from a second-set stumble to defeat China’s Fu Xiaofang, 4-1, 0-4, 4-1, while Amit recovered from a sluggish start to turn back Germany’s Ina Kaplan, 2-4, 4-1, 4-1. RuTheir victories arranged a second-round clash in the tournament’s double-elimination group stage, which was being played at press time. Interestingly, it was a rematch of last year’s finals where Centeno prevailed after a little more than three hours, 4-1, 2-4, 4-2, 3-4, 4-2. Both Filipinas are bidding for a historic third women’s 10-ball world title. Centeno previously ruled the event in 2023 and is seeking a successful title defense, while Amit won the inaugural championship in 2009 before adding a second crown in 2013. The tournament gathered 64 elite players offering a total pot of $200,000 (around P12.3 million) with $55,000 (around P3.3 million) to the winner.

Rescuers recover 3 bodies from Pakistan's Broad Peak avalanche. ISLAMABAD (AP) — Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak found four bodies and recovered three of them Friday, July 31, and were continuing to search for the other missing climbers despite adverse weather that hampered helicopter flights, officials said. A statement from the regional Gilgt-Baltistan government identified the three recovered bodies as Nepalese climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed and American climber Mallory Geis. It said the bodies had been transported to a hospital. The announcement came hours after officials said search teams had located the remains of four climbers despite harsh weather. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media. They did not immediately identify the fourth body that had been spotted. Bad weather continued to hamper the rescue effort Friday, according to a statement from the Gilgit-Baltistan region's Chief Minister Amjad Hussain. The climbers lost contact with their base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak while they were attempting to scale the mountain, said Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan. “The team has been out of communication since Thursday,” said Haidri, adding that army helicopters were part of the search-and-rescue operation. Authorities said the search for the missing climbers continued until Friday evening and would resume Saturday. According to the Alpine Club, the expedition comprised five Nepali climbers in addition to the Omani and American climbers, as well as Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and one other foreign climber. On Friday, China’s government said it was trying to verify whether any of its nationals were among the 10 climbers missing. “We will provide assistance to Chinese citizens in need and are also willing to offer help in accordance with the needs of the Pakistani side,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Friday in Beijing. The expedition leader was the renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born former soldier in the British army widely known as Nims Dai. He climbed the world’s 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary, “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible.” His record was surpassed in 2023. Moving Mountains, a travel company based in Pakistan, announced late last month that the expedition team was on its way to the small town of Askole and wished them a safe journey climbing Broad Peak. The company said this was Geis’ first try at an 8,000-meter peak in Pakistan, while it was expected to be Sakhi’s final one. Sakhi is a guide for the company, as well as a geographer and high-altitude photographer, and has climbed some of the world’s major peaks, according to Moving Mountains’ website. Geis, 39, lives in San Antonio. She announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her Pilates studio to take “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved.” Broad Peak, at 8,047 meters (26,401 feet), is the world’s 12th-highest mountain. It lies in Pakistan’s Karakoram range, home to five of the world’s 14 peaks above 8,000 meters, attracting climbers from around the globe. Accidents are common during climbing expeditions in northern Pakistan because of avalanches and rapidly changing weather.

Luxury, revisited: Amorita's next chapter in Palawan. Allow me to sing my praises to One-Of Collection—the boutique hospitality management group behind Amorita Resort, Momo Beach House, and The Funny Lion—which, as a young lifestyle journalist more than a decade ago, introduced me to what real luxury Filipino hospitality is all about. I can think of only a handful of local hospitality companies that consistently match this group's level of service, accommodations, and destinations. It was the 2010s, and as a young writer, I was cutting my teeth on the local travel beat. I was assigned to explore Bohol's lesser-known destinations. We ventured to the northern reaches of the island, from the stepped farms of the Cadapdapan Rice Terraces in Candijay, reminiscent of those in the Cordilleras, all the way to Ubay, with its eco-agritourism sites, picturesque dams, and beaches. Throughout the trip, we stayed in modest provincial accommodations, comfortable enough, with trademark Filipino hospitality, and were served good honest provincial fare, with the occasional lechon to my delight. Toward the end of the journey, our local government hosts casually mentioned that a major resort in Panglao was supporting their efforts to promote Bohol tourism, and that we would spend our final nights there. That was my first stay at Amorita Resort Bohol. The contrast between it and the modest inns we had stayed in throughout the trip was striking. I even wrote in my newspaper article that the villa assigned to me looked "straight out of a Taschen architecture coffee table book." The architecture, the interiors, the impeccable service, the food, and the villa with its own lap pool left my young writer's mind completely blown. So this is what a Filipino hospitality brand can do, I remember thinking. It could go toe to toe with the best international resorts. I was pampered to no end. Now, years later and far more seasoned on the lifestyle beat, I thought I had seen it all and tasted it all. So when an invitation arrived to visit the newly opened Amorita Resort and Spa in Puerto Princesa, Palawan, I assumed it would simply be a larger, newer version of the Bohol property. I was wrong. The new resort immediately impresses with its confident architectural language. Set along a secluded mangrove-lined shoreline overlooking the Sulu Sea, the property embraces expansive open spaces, earth-toned materials, and seamless indoor-outdoor transitions that allow nature to become part of the experience rather than just the backdrop. The restrained palette of grays, generous volumes, long horizontal lines, and cantilevered forms give the resort an unmistakably contemporary character—positively international moderne. There are unmistakable Brutalist influences throughout the property too, softened by lush landscaping and natural light. Walking through its corridors repeatedly reminded us of Frank Lloyd Wright's principle of compression and release, where enclosed passages suddenly open into expansive spaces overlooking gardens, pools, and the sea. The effect makes every arrival feel calculated, allowing the architecture to reveal itself gradually instead of all at once. Our villa could only be described as indulgent, yet restrained in design. The generous living area, soaring ceilings, and thoughtfully planned bathroom with separate his-and-her vanities all contribute to a feeling of spaciousness. Beyond the bedroom is an enclosed outdoor area where a large soaking tub sits beside a wooden daybed, creating a private sanctuary where you can bask in the sun without leaving your villa. And yes, there is also a private dipping pool. The property's Palawan Pool Villas measure 109 square meters and include two gardens, further reinforcing the sense of privacy. The resort itself extends well beyond its accommodations. In addition to its suites and villas, guests have access to two swimming pools, a full-service spa, a fitness center, and event spaces that can accommodate up to 200 guests, making it equally suited for leisure escapes, weddings, and corporate retreats. The food is every bit as elevated as the accommodations. Dining revolves around two distinct restaurants. Katala, the all-day dining restaurant named after Palawan's critically endangered cockatoo, interprets Filipino cuisine through a contemporary Asian lens using regional flavors and locally sourced ingredients. Turchino, meanwhile, offers a more intimate Italian dining experience centered on handcrafted pastas, responsibly sourced seafood, and refined takes on Mediterranean classics. Among Katala's standouts were the coconut-infused Sambal Ceviche brightened with pineapple green chili sambal and pomelo, the crisp Ocean Fritte loaded with fresh seafood, and the beautifully layered Katala Cake made with purple yam crème caramel, cassava flan cake, and cheese tuile. The menu also features dishes such as Tamarind Beef, Pork Belly Rendang, Jackfruit Mahi, and Inasal ala Puebla, reflecting both Filipino flavors and broader Asian influences. Still, my favorite discovery came not from the kitchen but from the bar. The Frozen Colada quickly became my drink of choice. Blended with white rum, coconut rum, pineapple, and coconut cream, it was refreshing without being overly sweet and had just enough alcohol to keep the mood light. Before long, the staff had caught on. I had one with lunch, another during dinner, and yet another while lounging by the pool under the midday Palawan sun on our final afternoon. Some trips are remembered through landmarks or photographs. I'll probably remember this one through a Frozen Colada. Of course, Puerto Princesa offers no shortage of things to do. You can spend the day island hopping in Honda Bay, take the boat through the Puerto Princesa Underground River, wander among the fireflies of the Iwahig River, explore the mangrove forests, or simply make your way around the city's seafood restaurants and local markets. But for me, I never felt the urge to leave. Perhaps that's because, over the years, this job has taken me to nearly every corner of Puerto Princesa. I've explored its islands, written about its attractions, and returned often enough that this trip didn't feel like another assignment to tick off a list of destinations. Instead, it became something far rarer in my line of work: an opportunity to slow down. Between mornings by the pool, long meals at Katala and Turchino, afternoons with a Frozen Colada in hand, and evenings spent watching the light fade over the Sulu Sea, I found that the resort itself was enough. More than a decade after Amorita first showed a young travel writer what Filipino luxury hospitality could be, its Puerto Princesa home reminded me why I never forgot that first stay—and why I'm still a journalist, still excited with new things to try and discover.

Flexible office market enters a new phase of growth. In 2026, the global shared office spaces market is valued at $72.56 billion, with Asia Pacific as the largest and fastest-growing market, based on the International Workplace Group (IWG) Global Workplace Survey. The flexible workspace market is estimated to grow by 600 percent by 2030, with an estimated value of $112.51 billion. Thirty-five percent of all office space will evolve to hybrid workspace in the same period, while 74 percent of companies are planning a full shift to flexible working. In Metro Manila, there are more than 230 co-working spaces. The office and co-work footprint in the country is around 560,000 to 600,000 sqm, according to Lobien Realty Group. For the first half of 2026, Colliers Philippines reported a 100 percent increase in the net take-up of 6,000 units in flexible spaces versus 3,000 in the same period last year. “Flexible workspaces are experiencing significant growth in uptake nationwide, driven by hybrid work models, connectivity, cost pressures on traditional office leasing, and corporate reassessments of strategies,” said Rowena B. Natividad, IWG country manager. She further explained that as infrastructure connects more cities, towns, and regional hubs, companies are looking for agile real estate solutions that allow them to scale quickly. Expanding beyond traditional CBDs Beyond traditional Manila CBDs, operators are expanding into regional and fringe markets (Clark, Baguio, Batangas, Pampanga, Cavite, Laguna, Iloilo, Cebu, and Davao), reflecting growing interest from businesses seeking proximity to talent and decentralized work hubs. Flexible workspaces are enabling the decentralization of work and supporting the rise of a more connected, hybrid economy. “The shift is clear: Over 60 percent of our 2025 expansion is outside traditional central business districts (CBDs), reflecting growing demand for flexible, accessible workplaces closer to where people live and businesses are expanding. While CBDs remain important for headquarters and corporate presence, businesses are increasingly adopting a hub-and-spoke approach—maintaining central offices while expanding into talent-ready satellite locations,” said Natividad. “The continued adoption of hybrid work is one of the key drivers of this shift. Colliers data shows that 82 percent of Filipino companies have adopted hybrid work models, ahead of Singapore at 55 percent and Australia at 56 percent,” she added. Benefits above traditional setups Natividad underscored that flexible workspaces address businesses' need for agility and scalability. “These plug-and-play solutions allow companies to focus on their core operations instead of managing leases, fit-outs, permits, and multiple vendors. As a service-based solution rather than a traditional lease, flexible workspace can help companies manage balance sheet liabilities more effectively.” In startups and small teams, the support comes through scalable private offices and collaborative coworking environments, enabling them to grow or downsize easily. Moreover, they can access meeting rooms and business services, and establish a professional presence without the cost and rigidity of traditional leases. By bringing workplaces closer to where people live, flexible workspaces help reduce travel time, improve work-life balance, and support stronger local communities. Beyond business benefits, it supports sustainability with more accessible workplace options, such as IWG’s growing network nationwide, while helping companies attract and retain talent as hybrid work becomes a key employee consideration and expanding access to a broader talent pool. “At the same time, we are creating new opportunities for property owners. Through our management agreement model, landlords retain ownership of their assets while IWG manages operations, marketing, and customer acquisition—providing a lower-risk way to activate underutilized assets and create new revenue opportunities.” Making flexible work more accessible IWG is leading the shift, with 50 operating locations totaling 54,000 sqm and more than 50 additional locations signed. Spaces at The Stiles Enterprise Plaza, located in Circuit, Makati City, is the latest addition. Together with Instant Group, their combined portfolio now reaches 92,000 sqm across 55 locations. In the pipeline for the year, IWG brands Signature, Regus, and HQ will be launched in key locations such as Ortigas, BGC, San Fernando in Pampanga, Mactan in Cebu, and Batangas City. Another important milestone is the opening of Humanly APECO in Casiguran, Aurora, IWG's first venture in health care. By expanding into these regional hubs, IWG is helping businesses access talent, but also supporting local economic growth.

Sam Fender, Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ becomes longest-running UK No. 1 single in chart history. Sam Fender and Olivia Dean have made UK chart history after their hit collaboration "Rein Me In" became the longest-running No. 1 single in the country's history. The song has now spent 19 weeks at the top of the Official UK Singles Chart, surpassing the previous record of 18 weeks set by Frankie Laine's "I Believe" in 1953. The milestone ends one of the longest-standing records in British music. Other blockbuster hits that came close but fell short include Bryan Adams' "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You," which spent 16 weeks at No. 1 in 1991, Wet Wet Wet's "Love Is All Around" with 15 weeks in 1994, Drake's "One Dance" with 15 weeks in 2016, and Ed Sheeran's "Shape of You," which topped the chart for 14 weeks in 2017. Reacting to the achievement, Fender said he was "completely lost for words," thanking Dean and fans for turning the song into what he described as "the juggernaut that it is." Originally written for Fender's 2025 album "People Watching," "Rein Me In" was initially released as an album track. It gained new momentum after being re-recorded as a duet with Dean, who added a new verse from the perspective of the woman left behind in the song's narrative. The duet version was released in June 2025 and took 36 weeks to climb to No. 1. Since reaching the summit in February, it has repeatedly returned to the top after brief interruptions by releases from Harry Styles, Olivia Rodrigo, Ariana Grande and Taylor Swift. Its success is particularly notable because it came despite the UK's "accelerated decline" chart rule, introduced in 2017 to prevent older songs from dominating the rankings for extended periods. Under the system, streams are given reduced weight after a song has spent at least 10 weeks on the chart and experiences consecutive declines in streaming. This week, "Rein Me In" held off Shakira and Burna Boy's official FIFA World Cup song "Dai Dai," which remained at No. 2. The collaboration also won Song of the Year at the 2026 BRIT Awards, further cementing its status as one of the biggest British hits of the decade.

An existential Spidey & coffee cup memories. Starring a now 30-year-old Tom Holland and directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" has taken off globally in a big way, single-handedly proving that the superhero film genre still has life in it despite the box office disappointment of "Supergirl" in June. And when one considers that "Spider-Man: No Way Home" was supposed to be the concluding chapter of a Tom Holland-led trilogy, it's encouraging to find that, five years after its 2021 release, enthusiasm for a Spidey film has not diminished. Think about it. As a fresh-faced 20-year-old, Tom Holland first donned the Spidey mask in 2016's "Captain America: Civil War," marking his official entry into the Marvel Cinematic Universe. That was followed by his first standalone outing, "Spider-Man: Homecoming," two "Avengers" films, the second "Spider-Man" movie, an appearance in "Venom: Let There Be Carnage," and the aforementioned 2021 hit "No Way Home." That's a full decade of portraying the same character. So while the initial worldwide box office figures showed avid interest in the new film, there was the lingering question of whether "Brand New Day" actually deserves the acclaim and takes the Spider-Man narrative somewhere substantial and unexpected. Unexpected might be asking for too much, but I'm happy to report that there's a fresh veneer of maturity, vulnerability, and emotional heft to this 2026 iteration of Peter Parker. It definitely nudges the franchise in the right direction after the somewhat ambivalent way the trilogy conclude. I'm not going to talk about the plot points of this film because its beauty lies in experiencing the moments as they unfold. What I can say is that Holland, Zendaya as MJ, and Jacob Batalon as Ned continue to provide the strong emotional core of this installment. I'd even go so far as to say that Zendaya serves as the emotional fulcrum for much of the film's dramatic weight. You'll love the sequences in which Peter and Ned showcase just how much of science nerds and movie geeks they are, even referencing two other major film franchises that the pair would undoubtedly have adored. These moments make their "best friends" relationship feel authentic and genuinely heartfelt. There's a bounty of Easter eggs and references throughout the film. My title refers to just one of them: a coffee cup that first appeared at the start of "No Way Home." I'm certain Holland fans and Marvel devotees will have a field day spotting all these hidden details. While Mark Ruffalo and Florence Pugh make welcome cameo appearances as their familiar MCU characters, I'd single out Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle and "Stranger Things" star Sadie Sink as the film's two most enjoyable revelations. Sink truly sinks her teeth into her mystery role, and I can only hope we'll be seeing more of her in the forthcoming "Avengers" film and future MCU projects. So yes, we did need "Brand New Day" as a form of closure to Holland's Spider-Man era. Should Holland still return as Spidey in a future film? If only to pass the baton and do something similar to what Tony Stark did in helping establish Spider-Man, that would be great. But I wouldn't want to watch another full-length adventure featuring an aging Holland as Spider-Man. Where is Miles Morales in live-action form when we need him? Or Spider-Gwen? Although the poor reception for "Supergirl" may have dampened enthusiasm for that particular evolutionary path. In the meantime, there's so much to take in and enjoy with "Brand New Day." Come for the action sequences, which have never simulated the thrill of web-slinging more effectively, but stay for the heartfelt angst and existential pondering of your friendly neighborhood Spider-Man.

Old Swiss Inn returns to Manila with new Paco location. One of the Philippines' longest-standing restaurants is returning to the city where its story began. Old Swiss Inn will reopen on Aug. 8 at its new home in Manila's Paco district, marking a new chapter for the nearly 80-year-old restaurant after closing its longtime Makati City branch on July 1. The restaurant has relocated to the ground floor of the Garden Plaza Hotel & Suites at 1030 Belen St., beside the historic Paco Park. The move brings the establishment back to Manila, where its history is closely rooted. Known for introducing authentic Swiss cuisine to generations of Filipino diners, Old Swiss Inn will welcome guests from noon to 10 p.m., Monday through Saturday. The restaurant will be closed on Sundays. The new Paco location aims to preserve the restaurant's European culinary heritage while embracing the character of its historic surroundings. Situated next to one of Manila's best-known landmarks, the space offers a setting that reflects both the restaurant's legacy and the neighborhood's enduring charm. Ahead of its grand reopening, Old Swiss Inn will hold a soft opening from Aug. 3 to 7, giving diners an early look at its new Paco home. Guests who visit during the preview period will receive 20 percent off the restaurant's menu, including its premium steaks and signature Swiss specialties. With its reopening, Old Swiss Inn begins a new chapter while continuing the tradition that has made it a familiar name in the local dining scene for decades. Reservations may be made by calling 0918-999-1010 or by sending a direct message through its official social media channels.

Boy, 13, fatally stabbed by classmate inside Las Piñas school. A 13-year-old student was fatally stabbed by his 14-year-old classmate following an argument inside Las Piñas National High School on Friday afternoon, July 31. Las Piñas City Police chief Col. Fermin Armendarez identified the victim only by the alias “ADO,” a resident of Barangay Daniel Fajardo. He sustained a stab wound to the left side of his chest and was rushed to Las Piñas District Hospital, where he was declared dead while undergoing treatment. The suspect, identified only as “MJE,” a resident of Barangay Talon Dos, was taken into custody and later turned over to the Bahay Pag asa youth care facility operated by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), in line with procedures for children in conflict with the law. Police said the incident happened around 4:30 p.m. on the fourth floor of the school, in front of Room 401. Initial investigation showed the two students argued during recess, allegedly over change from a bottled water purchase at the school canteen. Authorities said the suspect then drew a balisong (folding knife) and stabbed the victim once in the chest before school personnel and responding officers intervened. Investigators are still determining the circumstances surrounding the incident and the events that led to the fatal stabbing. In a statement, Las Piñas National High School expressed condolences to the victim’s family and assured students, teachers, and staff that psychological first aid, counseling, and other psychosocial interventions would be provided. School officials said they are coordinating closely with local authorities and other concerned agencies as the investigation continues.

Katrina Llegado wins Miss Supranational 2026 crown in Poland. Katrina Llegado was crowned Miss Supranational 2026 during the pageant's coronation night held Friday in Nowy Sącz, Poland. The victory makes Llegado the second Filipina to win the international title after Mutya Datul, who claimed the crown in 2013. Llegado bested 66 other contestants from around the world and succeeded Brazil's Eduarda Braum as the new Miss Supranational. During the final question-and-answer round, contestants were asked when they stopped trying to become the woman the world expected them to be and instead chose to become their authentic selves. "I always believe that we should never fit into a mold. We are perfectly imperfect. I am someone who struggles with perfection, but I am here today doing my best, and becoming my best version. And here in Miss Supranational, I know I belong. I know a place for me, and this is becoming Supra, above and beyond," Llegado said. Llegado is no stranger to international pageantry. She represented the Philippines at Reina Hispanoamericana 2019 in Bolivia, where she finished as fifth runner-up. She earned the right to compete in Miss Supranational after finishing as a finalist in Miss Universe Philippines 2025, a competition won by Ahtisa Manalo. Before leaving for Poland, she relinquished her national title to Allyson Hetland in May. Hetland later advanced to the Top 7 of Miss Universe Philippines 2026. France's Eve Gilles finished as first runner-up, while Brazil's Lara Marina was named second runner-up. Nigeria's Ndah Eno placed third runner-up, and Karolina Gorylova of the Czech Republic completed the Top 5 as fourth runner-up.

FASHION PULIS: Talkative boy. When a breakup ends, both parties are expected to let go and move on. However, Talkative Boy (TB) seems unable to stop revisiting what happened with his Past Lover (PL). A few years ago, TB and PL kept their relationship low-key. Since they belonged to different television networks, keeping things private was understandable. But everything fell apart when TB allegedly discovered something PL had been hiding from him. At the time, TB was still trying to carve out his place in show business, while PL's career was already on the rise. Both were talented actors, but PL enjoyed an early advantage, backed by a strong management team and an aggressive publicity machine that quickly made her a household name. TB, meanwhile, was being groomed as a versatile performer, effortlessly shifting from comedy to drama from one project to the next. Just when many believed their relationship was thriving, an unexpected incident changed everything. While waiting for his turn on a show, TB noticed that PL had left her phone unattended. Unable to resist, he picked it up and scrolled through its contents. Although many would consider it an invasion of privacy, TB allegedly stumbled upon messages that convinced him PL had not been honest with him. According to the story, the messages contained references to intimate moments that left TB devastated. Overcome with emotion, he reportedly left the phone open so PL would know he had seen everything. The incident rattled him so much that he was no longer able to perform. Years have passed since the breakup, but TB continues to talk about the failed relationship whenever given the opportunity. Some observers believe his repeated public comments suggest he has yet to fully move on. PL, for her part, has consistently denied cheating. Her career has continued to flourish, and she has largely stayed silent about her past relationship with TB, choosing not to publicly respond to his claims. "If talk is cheap, then being silent is expensive. And many people, it seems, can't afford to buy into it." — Anthony Liccione Loyalty and gratitude The main personalities involved have remained silent, but Minor Players (MP) have refused to let go of remarks allegedly made by Popular Personality (PP) and believed to be directed at Another Personality (AP). PP is known for her creativity and built her career from the ground up. She rose from relative obscurity to become one of the industry's most influential figures through hard work, steering clear of gambling endorsements and similar ventures. Along the way, she collaborated with several high-profile celebrities, and those partnerships helped further elevate her profile. The controversy began during one of PP's usual lighthearted exchanges with another celebrity. In the course of their banter, PP made a remark that MP interpreted as a subtle jab at AP. Others, however, felt the comment was too vague to be linked to anyone in particular, especially since AP chose not to respond publicly. The issue escalated when MP openly criticized PP. According to MP, AP had played an important role in PP's early career, making the alleged remark appear ungrateful. MP also made it clear they were standing up for AP, demonstrating their loyalty and willingness to defend someone they believe deserves recognition. Whether PP's statement was really intended for AP remains unclear, but the exchange has reignited conversations about gratitude, loyalty, and remembering those who helped along the way. "Be grateful for what you already have while you pursue your goals. If you aren't grateful for what you already have, what makes you think you would be happy with more?" — Roy T. Gun-wielding man nabbed in QC after fight with wife. A 47-year-old man was arrested Thursday night, July 30, after allegedly brandishing a homemade firearm and threatening residents in Barangay Bagong Pag-asa, Quezon City, following a quarrel with his wife. Police said the suspect came out of his house carrying a homemade firearm, shouting in a scandalous manner that caused panic among residents who were chatting nearby. Authorities said the suspect allegedly aimed the weapon at several residents, who sought assistance from personnel of the District Mobile Force Battalion stationed in the area. Responding officers immediately arrested the suspect at around 9 p.m. and recovered an improvised firearm and one live 12-gauge shotgun shell from his possession. Police said records showed the suspect had previous cases for alarms and scandals, resistance and disobedience to a person in authority, and grave threats. The suspect is facing complaints for alarms and scandals, grave threats, and violation of Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, before the Quezon City Prosecutor's Office.

Escudero eyes tobacco-style ban on gambling ads, endorsements. Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero has filed a bill seeking to prohibit gambling advertisements and sponsorships across the country, saying tighter regulation is needed to address the growing risks of compulsive gambling and shield minors and other vulnerable sectors from aggressive marketing. Under Senate Bill (SB) No. 2347, gambling promotions would be barred from television, radio, print, online platforms, and social media. The proposal would also ban celebrity endorsements and influencer marketing tied to gambling services, while requiring authorized consumer communications to include responsible gambling advisories. Escudero said the proposal follows the framework used to regulate tobacco advertising under Republic Act (RA) No. 9211 or the Tobacco Regulation Act of 2003, which imposed broad restrictions on tobacco promotions to protect public health. “It’s about time that we regulate the gambling industry the same way we regulated tobacco two decades ago,” he said upon filing the measure, noting that both industries pose serious risks when advertising becomes widespread and targets young people. The senator pointed out that RA No. 9211—which he supported during his time in the House of Representatives—banned tobacco advertisements in print, broadcast, electronic, and outdoor media, while also prohibiting celebrity endorsements and product placements in entertainment content. He said those measures helped reduce tobacco exposure among minors and non-adult smokers. Escudero said his proposal would build on recent efforts by the Ad Standards Council (ASC), which issued a voluntary self-regulation circular directing its members to remove gambling imagery and related materials from media platforms. “My bill shall institutionalize this effort by placing the restrictions under a national legal framework, ensuring uniform enforcement and preventing gaps in regulation,” he stressed. While recognizing the gambling industry's contribution to government revenues, employment, and tourism, Escudero said its rapid expansion has been accompanied by increasingly sophisticated advertising and marketing campaigns. He warned that the heightened visibility of gambling services “presents significant public mental and physical well-being and socioeconomic concerns, particularly with respect to undue exposure, excessive, compulsive, and irresponsible gambling behavior.” In the bill’s explanatory note, Escudero cited the continued growth of online and digital gaming, noting that the Philippine gambling industry generated P396.13 billion in gross gaming revenues in fiscal year 2025. He said the measure seeks to strike a balance between the industry's economic contributions and the need for stronger social safeguards by requiring gambling operators and advertisers to adhere to higher ethical standards. The bill also provides a one-year transition period after its enactment, allowing gambling operators, advertisers, and government agencies time to phase out existing promotional materials and comply with the new regulations before full enforcement begins. Violators would face increasing penalties, beginning with fines of up to P200,000 or imprisonment of up to one year for a first offense, P300,000 or up to two years for a second offense, and P500,000 or up to three years for a third offense. Repeat violations could also lead to the revocation of business permits or licenses, while foreign nationals found liable may face deportation. Escudero said the penalties are intended "only to ensure its effective implementation,” underscoring that deterrence is essential to protect public welfare and uphold the integrity of the law. Beyond advertising restrictions, the measure directs government agencies to conduct sustained public education campaigns on responsible gambling, mental health support, and consumer protection to help Filipinos make informed decisions. According to Escudero, the bill aims to “foster a more responsible gaming environment, protect minors and vulnerable persons, promote informed consumer choice, and advance public interest".

Speaker Dy ensures transparent 2027 national budget process. The House of Representatives will build on the pro-transparency measures introduced last year to ensure that the proposed 2027 national budget is responsive, accountable, and focused on the needs of the Filipino people. Thus, said House Speaker Faustino "Bojie" Dy III over the weekend following the launch of the LegisHear initiative in his hometown of Isabela. Speaking during a press briefing after the launch of LegisHear in Isabela, Dy said the House is ready to undertake its constitutional duty of scrutinizing the P7.2 trillion National Expenditure Program (NEP), which is expected to be transmitted by the Executive before Aug. 14. The NEP is the precursor to the enventual General Appropriations Act (GAA) or national budget. The Speaker said public consultations under the newly launched LegisHear program would complement the budget process by giving lawmakers a better understanding of the priorities and concerns of communities across the country before appropriations are finalized. Asked whether the House was considering additional reforms on top of those it adopted during the deliberations of the 2026 national budget, the Speaker said: "Wala pa naman kaming napag-uusapan, pero nakita naman natin na maayos naman, at nakita nating may reporma. Nakita rin natin na may transparency." (We have not discussed anything yet, but we saw that things are in order, and we saw reforms. We also saw transparency.) “Sa tingin ko, lalo pa nating bibigyan ng mahahalagang security measures upang matiyak na ang ating ipapasa na 2027 budget ay talagang maayos." (In my view, we will further provide important security measures to ensure that the 2027 budget we pass is truly sound.) Dy said the House remains committed to preserving the reforms the chamber instituted to ensure transparency and accountability in the appropriations process, while continuing to improve safeguards that protect the integrity of the national budget. Under Dy's leadership, the House pursued a series of budget reforms, including greater transparency in the appropriations process. These include the Budget Amendments and Review Subcommittee (BARSc) and the livestreaming of the budget bicameral committee deliberations. Focused on work, with or without surveys The House chief says congressmen remain focused on fulfilling their constitutional mandate and on crafting responsive legislation. Dy says their work is guided not by survey ratings but by the needs and sentiments of the Filipino people. “Trabaho lang kami. With or without the survey, nakita ninyo kami sa Kongreso. Nakita ninyo kaming tahimik na nagtatrabaho. Ginagawa po namin ang aming mga responsibilidad, at nakikita po namin ang aming mga priorities na dapat naming isulong sa bawat Kongreso.” (We are just working. With or without the survey, you saw us in Congress. You saw us quietly working. We are fulfilling our responsibilities, and we see the priorities we must advance in every Congress.) Dy expressed gratitude for the public’s continued trust in the House, and said the institution’s priority has always been to earn that trust through consistent work and meaningful reforms. “Salamat. Ibig sabihin, hindi naman po kami after sa ganoong mga rating, pero salamat sa pagtitiwala. Kasi kung maaalala ninyo, noong ako ay unang na-elect, talagang ang aming pinagsusumikapan, sa suporta at tulong ng bawat miyembro, ay maibalik ang tiwala ng ating mga kababayan,” the Speaker said. (Thank you. This means we are not after such ratings, but thank you for the trust. Because if you recall, when I was first elected, what we really worked hard for—with the support and help of every member—was to restore the trust of our people.) The former Isabela governor noted that rebuilding confidence in Congress has been a continuing effort, with lawmakers choosing to focus on legislation that addresses the everyday concerns of Filipinos rather than public perception. “Kaya naman patuloy po kaming nagsusumikap hanggang ngayon. Alam po namin na marami pa ring pagkukulang, kaya ito ay isang bahagi na nakikita namin upang lalo pang mapaganda at mapalapit tayo, at malaman natin ang tunay na sentimyento ng ating mga kababayan para lalo pang maging maganda ang mga batas na ihahain natin para sa ating bansa,” he stressed. (That is why we continue to strive until now. We know there are still many shortcomings, so this is part of what we see as a way to further improve, to draw closer, and to understand the true sentiment of our people so that the laws we present for our country will be better.)
