The Met’s next fashion exhibit spotlights John Galliano, and will confront his troubled past. The next Met Gala fashion exhibit will be devoted to a designer famed for both his singular talent and the scandal that lost him one of the top posts in all of fashion: John Galliano. The British designer was creative director at Christian Dior for nearly 15 years, the very pinnacle of the fashion world, before he made a series of antisemitic and racist comments in 2010 and 2011 that went viral, leading to his conviction in an antisemitism trial. Dropped by Dior, he spent several years involved in public and private efforts to rehabilitate. He made a comeback in 2014 when he was hired by Paris fashion house Maison Margiela, where he remained for a decade. Now, he'll become only the third living designer to be the subject of a solo show at the Costume Institute of the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Long a red carpet favorite for his flamboyant, even fantastical style, John and his creations should make for an intensely watched carpet at next May’s Met Gala, which every year launches the spring exhibit at the Costume Institute. Not surprisingly, the museum is taking pains to emphasize that the exhibit will not shy away from the problematic aspects of John’s history. “Alongside Galliano’s extraordinary creative accomplishments, the exhibition will address the derogatory conduct that fundamentally altered his career and public reception,” said a statement issued by the museum. “In doing so, the exhibition will consider how artistic achievement should be understood alongside ethical accountability.” The show’s main curator, Andrew Bolton, who curates nearly all the Met’s big fashion exhibits, noted that the exhibit “considers both how Galliano has remapped the world through fashion and how his conduct, its consequences, and changing cultural values have reshaped our understanding of his work.” Even so, organizers had to tread carefully when planning the show. Preparation included meetings with Jewish community leaders in New York to gauge their feelings, the museum said, confirming a report in The New York Times. Those meetings included Andrew, John, and Anna Wintour, the Vogue editor who masterminds the Met Gala every year. The show will be organized into three parts, the museum said. The first, “Bearings," will “directly address the rupture caused by his antisemitic, racist, and anti-Asian conduct in 2010 and 2011, which resulted in his dismissal from Christian Dior and his eponymous label and his conviction by a Paris court for public insults based on race, religion, ethnicity, or origin," the museum said. It will also deal with his treatment for substance addiction and later public acknowledgment of his actions. The second, “Horizons,” will examine the designer's sources of inspiration, such as history, geography, art, storytelling, and performance. And the third, “Atlas of Transformation,” will focus on "Galliano’s creativity, craftsmanship, experimentation, and technical innovation," the museum said. The 2024 documentary “High and Low—John Galliano” suggests John was overworked and abusing alcohol and drugs when he made a series of antisemitic and racist comments in 2010 and 2011. A video of him saying “I love Hitler" in a bar went viral. The Times quoted Jonathan Greenblatt, chief executive of the Anti-Defamation League, as saying of the planned show: “We believe John Galliano has genuinely worked through the issues that led to his antisemitic outburst years ago in Paris, and we have long since accepted his apology." "His efforts to repair the damage his words caused and to learn from that incident should be applauded.” The show, “John Galliano: Horizons,” will run from May 9, 2027, through Jan. 9, 2028. (Jocelyn Noveck/AP)

Las Piñas, Meralco eye wider use of renewable energy. The Las Piñas City government and the Manila Electric Company (Meralco) are strengthening their partnership to expand the use of renewable energy and provide residents with cleaner, more affordable electricity. Meralco officials paid a courtesy call on Mayor April Aguilar last Friday, July 31, at the Las Piñas City Hall, where they discussed initiatives to accelerate renewable energy adoption in the city. Among the proposals were measures to fast-track the installation of solar energy systems, streamline the processing of residential net metering applications, and promote programs that could lower electricity costs and reduce the carbon footprint of Las Piñeros. City officials highlighted Las Piñas’ strong performance in renewable energy adoption. A recent report shows the city ranks third nationwide in commissioned residential net metering (NM) installations, with 1,170 residential connections and a total installed capacity of 7.7 megawatt peak (MWp). Net metering allows homeowners with solar photovoltaic systems to export excess electricity to the distribution grid, offsetting their consumption and reducing monthly bills. Aguilar said the city government remains committed to working with stakeholders to implement programs that promote energy efficiency, sustainability, and affordable power services for residents. She added that the partnership with Meralco supports the city’s continuing efforts to encourage renewable energy use while building a cleaner, more resilient, and environmentally sustainable Las Piñas.

Infantino abandoned World Cup equity plan after seismic FIFA backlash. Here's what to know. GENEVA (AP) — Gianni Infantino truly looked the “King of Soccer,” as U.S. President Donald Trump likes to call him, as the two allies sat together watching the World Cup final less than two weeks ago. Sure, there were some boos inside MetLife Stadium near New York, when the two men walked across the turf to present the trophy and medals to Spain and Argentina players on July 19. Still, that 104th and final game capped a biggest-ever tournament seen as a vindication for the FIFA president — a consensus success on the field and a financial bonanza for global soccer. Infantino could look ahead to his likely reelection coronation next March. The sunny scene must now feel an age ago since Infantino caused a seismic rift in global soccer. The intensifying fallout has threatened the 56-year-old Infantino's job after he seemed untouchable until this week. Infantino's misstep was inviting private investors, led by Joshua Kushner, to buy a stake in future profits from World Cups and all FIFA events. The ensuing backlash — which included vows by European nations to boycott FIFA events and claims from senior staff that Infantino deceived everyone — led Infantino to announce Friday that he was abandoning the plan. “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” he said in a statement. Infantino left New York City last week with letters pledging election support from about 200 of FIFA’s 211 national member federations who vote for their leader every four years. Now, even after scrapping his divisive investment project, his support remains unclear at best. What would the plan have done? Infantino's proposal would have created a subsidiary — known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) — for the money-making parts of the not-for-profit soccer body's work: Running tournaments like the World Cup, selling broadcasting and sponsorship, tickets and hospitality. Private equity and petrostate sovereign wealth money has been normalized in European club soccer, yet they still seem unthinkable for many observers in the World Cup — soccer's ultimate prize is about glory, not money, and fans have long believed the World Cup belongs to them. FIFA proposed raising $4.2 billion from investors buying stakes amounting to about 20% in FFE, based on an equity valuation of $20 billion. The “anchor investor” would have been Thrive Eternal, launched by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is a son-in-law of Trump. FIFA’s 211 member federations — already effective owners of the governing body as a nonprofit association under Swiss law — were offered $20 million each. The deadline to accept was Sept. 19. The members already are due $10 million each from FIFA over the next four years, funded largely by its record $15 billion revenue over 2023-26 tied to the World Cup just ended. FIFA says under FFE, that would have doubled to $20 million each, then rise to $22 million each through 2034, and $24 million to 2038. That’s a huge sum for tiny soccer federations in places like Andorra, Montserrat and Papua New Guinea. Deep-pocketed soccer powers like England, Spain or France have other priorities. Who lined up in opposition? Some FIFA vice presidents, some of FIFA’s top executives, all the European soccer federations, the soccer bodies of Asia and North America, Britain’s Prime Minister, the global group of national leagues, a lot of fans worldwide. Everyone, essentially. Infantino was looking increasingly friendless Friday. His senior adviser, former Goldman Sachs banker Carlos Cordeiro, resigned and called it a bad deal. FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour gave a stinging statement to The Associated Press in defense of colleagues that all but invited his boss to fire him. A key move Thursday was European soccer body UEFA vowing to boycott all FIFA competitions until Infantino dropped the plan. Europe’s teams routinely dominate and win FIFA trophies like the men’s World Cup and Club World Cup that are its biggest revenue earners. They collectively feared that private investors would seek — and demand — value from more games and bigger competitions that threaten the balance of global soccer. That could jeopardize attention and revenues for club soccer, including the Champions League. Fixture calendars are already congested, elite players are at their limits, broadcast and sponsor money is not unlimited. All are angry that Infantino seems not to have consulted anyone while planning the project over the last year, when he was so focused with spending time in Trump's orbit. Even Trump said Friday he had not spoken with the FIFA chief on his plan to sell stakes in the tournament. Did anyone support it? Infantino's traditional support base in Africa, which has 54 of the 211 voting members, had been neutral about the offers of game-changing money for many of them. The 10-nation South American group CONMEBOL said on Friday it had received the proposal and would evaluate the issue “with the rigor it demands.” CONMEBOL is led by FIFA vice president Alejandro Dominguez of Paraguay, who is relying on Infantino expanding the 2030 World Cup to 64 teams. That would give more games to minority co-hosts Argentina, Paraguay and inaugural 1930 World Cup host Uruguay, who currently are set to get just one game each of the 104. The rest are in Spain, Portugal and Morocco. What happens with Infantino? The UEFA-led resistance succeeded in stopping the sell-off plan. Will that satisfy Infantino's opponents to leave him in office? Does Infantino have the credibility to stay in office after interventions Friday by Lamour and Cordeiro that surely would make most presidencies untenable? Nov. 18 is the deadline for candidates to enter the next presidential contest, exactly four months ahead of the vote in Rabat, Morocco, where FIFA has its African headquarters. Infantino was reelected unopposed in 2019 in Paris and 2023 in Kigali, Rwanda. FIFA statutes allow him one more four-year term in office. The FFE spinoff seemed a way to create a commissioner-like role for Infantino beyond 2031, likely paying much more than his current annual salary and bonus deal of more than $6 million. It would take 106 votes to ensure a majority in a contested election. Continents surely do not vote uniformly en bloc, but most of Europe's 55, plus CONCACAF's 35 and Asia's 46 would be a solid base. Speculation on a likely direct challenger typically lands on Paris Saint-Germain's Qatari president Nasser al-Khelaïfi and the Canadian FIFA vice president Victor Montagliani. Such talk seemed fanciful until this week, despite long-term unease with Infantino's style and previous attempts to force through unpopular projects. The talk has never seemed more likely to become action.

Mark Villar pushes for LIGTAS Act after Las Piñas school stabbing. Senator Mark Villar has called for stronger school security measures following the fatal stabbing of a Grade 9 student inside Las Piñas National High School, saying the incident highlights the need for immediate action to protect students better. Villar described the killing as a tragic loss and stressed that schools should remain safe spaces for learning rather than places where students face threats to their lives. "Our schools must always be places of safety, learning, and hope—not places where our children are exposed to violence and danger. No student should ever have to fear for their safety while pursuing their education and dreams," Villar said. The senator expressed his sympathies to the victim's family and said his office is extending assistance to help them during this difficult time. He also urged local authorities and relevant government agencies to promptly investigate the incident, hold those responsible accountable, and strengthen school security to prevent similar cases. Villar likewise appealed to educators, parents, and communities to work together in fostering respect, empathy, and peaceful conflict resolution among young people. According to Villar, the tragedy underscores the urgency of passing his proposed Senate Bill (SB) No. 2321, or the Learning Institution's Guaranteed Threat Avoidance and Safety (LIGTAS) Act. The measure seeks to improve campus safety by increasing police visibility in schools, establishing coordinated threat assessment systems, creating direct emergency hotlines linked to police, fire, and rescue units, ensuring immediate notification of parents during emergencies, and requiring adequate first-aid equipment, trained medical personnel, and security guards. It also calls for the installation of strategically placed CCTV cameras, appropriate security screening systems, and regular safety and security training for students, teachers, and school personnel. "Hindi na natin maibabalik ang buhay na nawala dahil sa masakit na trahedyang ito, ngunit hindi tayo maaaring manatiling walang ginagawa. Kailangan nating kumilos nang maiwasan ang ganitong mga pangyayari at tiyaking ligtas ang bawat paaralan para sa ating mga anak. Ang bawat batang Pilipino ay may karapatang makapag-aral sa isang kapaligirang ligtas, protektado, at malaya mula sa anumang uri ng karahasan," Villar said. (We can no longer bring back the life lost in this heartbreaking tragedy, but we cannot afford to remain idle. We must take action to prevent incidents like this from happening again and ensure that every school is a safe place for our children. Every Filipino child has the right to study in an environment that is safe, protected, and free from all forms of violence.) A 13-year-old student was fatally stabbed by his 14-year-old classmate following an argument inside Las Piñas National High School on Friday afternoon, July 31.

Pacquiao stresses Mayweather rematch will be pro fight. Manny Pacquiao remains committed to facing Floyd Mayweather Jr. in a professional fight after their planned rematch was postponed. The 47-year-old boxing icon said Friday, July 31, that the bout is being rescheduled for early 2027 due to Mayweather’s prior commitments, including an exhibition fight this year. “Mayweather will have an exhibition [fight]... but our match next year will be a pro fight,” Pacquiao said in Filipino during the Maharlika Pilipinas Pickleball Tour press briefing, where he arrived three hours later than the scheduled time. Pacquiao’s camp previously said efforts were being made to arrange a non-professional bout for him later this year, but the eight-division world champion reiterated that his clash with Mayweather will be a legitimate professional contest. Pacquiao, who holds a 62-8-3 record, last fought professionally on July 19, 2025, when he drew with WBC welterweight champion Mario Barrios in Las Vegas. The highly anticipated rematch between Pacquiao and Mayweather, initially backed by streaming giant Netflix, was postponed after the American boxing legend became embroiled in a breach-of-contract lawsuit filed by CSI Sports Events.

Emergency water interruption hits Tondo, Binondo on Aug. 1. An emergency water supply interruption will affect parts of Manila on Saturday, Aug. 1, due to urgent repair works on a major pipeline. In an advisory, authorities said the shutdown is necessary to fix a defective 800-millimeter primary line gate valve located in the Muelle area. The service interruption is scheduled from 1 p.m. to 11 p.m. Affected areas include: -No water supply in parts of North Manila. -Low to no water pressure in Binondo and Tondo. Residents are advised to store enough water ahead of the scheduled repair and expect normalization of service after the completion of the works.

Mayor Isko calls vendors, orders Fusion Alley cleanup. Following complaints from a student over noise and sanitation at Fusion Alley, Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso summoned vendors and ordered a full cleanup of the popular food strip along Delos Reyes Street. A meeting was held on Friday, July 31, at Manila City Hall, where Domagoso personally addressed the vendors and reiterated city government policies on sanitation, proper waste disposal, and compliance with existing ordinances. He warned that repeated violations could lead to penalties, including possible closure of stalls. “Matapos nating marinig ang reklamo ng isang estudyante, agad po nating ipinatawag ang mga manininda sa Fusion Alley sa Sampaloc (After hearing the complaint of a student, we immediately called the Fusion Alley vendors in Sampaloc) ,” Domagoso said. The mayor said the city is not ignoring concerns from residents and students living near the area. “Hindi po natin binabalewala ang reklamo ng iilan. Nakisuyo po tayo sa mga manininda na panatilihing malinis ang lugar at iwasan ang sobrang ingay upang hindi makaperwisyo sa mga nakatira sa paligid (We are not disregarding the complaints of a few. We asked the vendors to keep the area clean and avoid excessive noise so they will not disturb nearby residents) ,” he said. As part of the cleanup, tents were temporarily removed to allow a more thorough flushing and cleaning of the area. Domagoso warned that vendors who fail to maintain cleanliness could face closure. “Malinaw ang aking bilin: kapag nakita kong marumi ang paligid ay kaagad ko silang ipapasara (My instruction is clear: if I see that the surroundings are dirty, I will immediately have them closed) ,” he said. He also directed the Department of Public Services (DEPS) to collect garbage from the area earlier. “Hindi lang po gobyerno ang may responsibilidad. Kailangan din ng kusang disiplina at pakikiisa ng bawat manininda (The government is not the only one responsible. Each vendor must also show discipline and cooperation) ,” Domagoso said. The mayor said the city’s goal is to maintain livelihood opportunities while ensuring cleanliness and order. "Ang hanap natin ay balanse, may kabuhayan ang ating mga kababayan, ngunit maayos at malinis pa rin ang kapaligiran (What we are looking for is balance, our people have livelihoods while the surroundings remain orderly and clean) ,” he said.

Pasay cops nab Chinese fugitive. A Chinese national on Pasay City’s most wanted list was arrested Friday, July 31, in a manhunt operation for violating the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Act of 2009. Pasay City Police chief Col. Joselito De Sesto identified the suspect only by his surname, Lin, 30. He was arrested at about 1:40 p.m. on F.B. Harrison Street in Barangay 70 by operatives of the Pasay City Police Warrant and Subpoena Section. De Sesto said the operation was part of the station’s intensified campaign against wanted persons and in compliance with standing warrants issued by the courts. The arrest was carried out by virtue of a warrant for service of sentence issued by Judge Iris Briones Laqui-Genilothe of the Pasay City Regional Trial Court Branch 111 in connection with a case for violation of the FDA Act of 2009. Police said the warrant carried no recommended bail. De Sesto said the successful operation underscores the Pasay City Police’s commitment to enforcing court orders and ensuring fugitives are held accountable. “We will continue to intensify our manhunt operations against wanted persons and work closely with the courts to ensure that justice is served,” he said. The suspect remains in the custody of the Pasay City Police pending his turnover to the court and the implementation of his sentence.

James Yap, Hua Siong keep FCAAI crown. Two-time PBA MVP James Yap, Rhagnee Sinco and Ken Bono starred in a decisive third quarter breakaway and Iloilo’s Hua Siong College defeated Xavier School, 72-57, in the rubber match to keep the 40-years division title in the Fil-Chinese Athletic Association Inc. (FCAAI) on Friday, July 31, at the FilOil EcoOil Centre in San Juan. Atoning for a dismal 9-point output in Game 2 where he missed all his 11 3-point attempts, Yap scored four of his game-high 23 points in the third which Bono and Sinco matched to turn a tight contest into another rout that extended their reign to another year. Yap’s triple to start off the payoff period proved to be the game changer as Lamtex Pipes-backed Hua Siong took a commanding 59-43 lead and never looked back. The Golden Stallions, backed by Powersox and AcroCity, did try to mount a comeback, but it was nipped in the bud by Yap and compony. Yap also had five rebound res and three assists in more than 32 minutes of action to win the Finals MVP award. The absence of former Rain or Shine star Chris Tiu due to a hamstring injury hurt Xavier’s bid the most as no one could provide the numbers the school icon routinely dished out in the past, including 17 in the team’s stunning 75-72 win in Game 1. Just like last season, Hua Siong won the series, 2-1. They forced a knockout match after a convincing 79-49 victory in Game 2. Held to just 8 points the last time after coming late in the game, Bono added 20 points and 16 boards while Sinco and tournament MVP Jaypee Belencion tallied 9 points each. Hounded by Hua Siong’s defenders right from the start, Joseph Yeo was held to just 12 points on 4-of-20 shooting. Bon Syiaco led Xavier with 16 points and 9 boards. Next for the league, which has the backing of Smart Sports, Tanduay Athletics, Genius Hardware, Ultraforce Tires, Cellboy, PGFlex Linoleum, Boysen, Lamtex Pipes, Jiang Nan, Hangry Pares, Powerhouse Tools, L.F. Fireworks, BYD Valenzuela, BAIC, Jetour, Yong Kee Roasting House, 1118 Autospa, and TCL, is the 45 years old division.

Manila forum revisits visual poetry, cites Filipino poet’s contributions. A literary forum in Manila revisited the work of Filipino poet Dr. Epitacio Ramos Tongohan, also known as Doc PenPen Bugtong Takipsilim, as part of discussions on visual poetry in the Philippines. The forum, held at the National Museum of the Filipino People in Manila, brought together scholars and cultural workers to examine the form, which combines text, symbols, and visual design. Visual poetry remains a niche practice in the country, with limited public platforms compared to more established forms such as spoken word and performance poetry. Tongohan, a physician by training, has promoted the form through publications and literary forums. Some literary circles refer to him as the “Father of Visual Poetry.” He was also cited in a recent recognition described as a “Prestige Father of Visual Poetry Award” in March 2026. FAMAS, which is primarily known as a film award-giving body, did not immediately provide further details on the citation. Participants in the forum said efforts are ongoing to document alternative literary forms and assess their place in contemporary Philippine literature.

Taguig police nab woman for falsification, 2 drug suspects. Police arrested a 63-year-old woman for falsification of public documents and two men for illegal drugs in Taguig City on Friday, July 31. Operatives of the Taguig police’s Station Warrant and Subpoena Section served a warrant of arrest against alias Florita in Barangay Tuktukan, Taguig. Florita was listed as the Southern Police District’s No. 4 most wanted person. The warrant was issued by the Taguig Regional Trial Court Branch 267 for 19 counts of falsification of public documents, with bail set at ₱72,000 per count or a total of ₱1.36 million. She was taken to the Taguig City Health Office for physical and medical examination before detention. In Barangay Pembo, Taguig, police arrested two newly identified street-level drug personalities in a buy-bust operation. The suspects were identified as alias Israel, 28, a tricycle driver, and alias Rommel, 39, a cook, both residents of Taguig. The operation was carried out by elements of the Station Drug Enforcement Unit and Police Sub-Station 10. An undercover officer purchased shabu from the suspects, leading to their arrest. Police seized eight plastic sachets containing 13.54 grams of shabu valued at ₱92,072, a .38-caliber revolver without a serial number loaded with three live rounds, and buy-bust money. The two will face complaints for violation of Sections 5 (sale of dangerous drugs) and 11 (possession of dangerous drugs) of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, and Republic Act 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act. Southern Police District director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco commended the teams for the operations.

Cone says Magnolia still formidable ahead of their ‘Clasico’ duel. Early results can be deceiving. Barangay Ginebra head coach Tim Cone knows that better than most, having spend decades in the PBA. For the multiple champion tactician, a slow start rarely defines a team’s true potential. That’s exactly what Con reminded to his players as the Kings clash with the Magnolia Hotshots still groping for form in the in the PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Sunday, Aug. 2. Game is at 7:30 p.m. with the two teams adding the first of the two chapters of their Manila Clasico rivalry in store for PBA fans in the eliminations of the season-ending conference. Providing a fitting appetizer is the clash between the streaking Rain or Shine and the undermanned Meralco at 5:15 p.m. Despite owning the better record in Group B, Cone believes Magnolia is playing better than its win-loss mark suggests and could be poised for a big run after a couple of near victories in their last few games. “Not struggling as much as we are. These early results in conferences, I think we make too big of a deal of them,” said Cone as the Kings hold on to a 2-2 record while the Hotshots are currently at the bottom with a 1-4 slate. “I remember one time when TNT got beat by, like, 15 points in their first game and then 19 points in the second game, and everybody was like nothing. And then they go on a seven-game winning streak, go into the finals and sweep the finals. I remember in our grand slam year with Alaska, we came out and lost our first three games. And then we won our next 11 straight. So, you know, early results are early results,” he added. For Cone, his team should remain laser focused against the Hotshots, who he believes has the talent and coaching wits to just simply turn things around. “You always want to get ahead. You always want to be on top of the standings. But, you know, you don't panic when you don't. And I don't think Magnolia is going to panic,” said Cone. “I know L.A. I know what kind of personality he has. He's not a guy who panics. They're going to figure it out. And hopefully they figure it out after we play them on Sunday,” he added.

Bomogao delivers KO win over Thai foe, secures $100k contract. Islay Erika Bomogao proved she is more than just a charming rising star, punching her ticket to ONE Championship with a stunning knockout victory over hometown fighter Klinphaka Por Thaisong in their atomweight Muay Thai bout at ONE Friday Fights 164 on Friday, Aug. 1, at Lumpinee Boxing Stadium. Bomogao went toe-to-toe with her Thai rival through the opening two rounds before finishing in emphatic fashion, delivering a crushing right hook that landed on Thaisong's jaw in the third and final round to seal the knockout with 2:48 remaining. The 25-year-old Team Bagsik standout stayed unbeaten at 5-0, while handing Thaisong her first defeat to drop to 1-1. The victory marked Bomogao's third knockout in five professional wins and earned the Baguio City native a coveted ONE Championship contract worth $100,000 (around P6.1 million), along with a THB350,000 (about P641,000) performance bonus. “I don’t know what to say. I’m just really happy and thankful. Thank you so much to everybody who has been part of my journey, especially my team,” an emotional Bomogao said. The Southeast Asian Games Muay Thai champion added patience was the key to breaking down her opponent. “I didn’t want to rush things. In the first and second rounds, I was trying to measure her,” Bomogao said. “My coaches told me to throw the straight hand, then get out of the way. I let my right hand go, and she went down,” she added.

Ombudsman suspends acting San Pablo City mayor for 6 months. SAN PABLO CITY, Laguna – The Office of the Ombudsman on July 31 suspended acting Mayor Justin Colago here for six months over a complaint filed by suspended Mayor Arcadio Gapangada Jr. on April 27. The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) will implement the order against Colago for conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service, grave abuse of authority, and grave misconduct. “The Ombudsman found sufficient grounds to place Colago under preventive suspension in connection with charges for grave abuse of authority, grave misconduct, and conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service,” the DILG said. Gapangada alleged that Colago “certified and signed appointment papers, daily time records, accomplishment reports, and payroll documents for a job order worker.” Colago will be replaced by Councilor Carmela Acebedo in an acting capacity. Gapangada was suspended following Colago’s complaint that he allegedly transferred and stripped city officials and employees of their functions to accommodate job order workers.

PM Vargas takes stab at amending EPIRA, halting pass-on charges to consumers. Proposals to amend the much-maligned Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) are beginning to snowball in the House of Representatives. This, after House Deputy Majority Leader Quezon City 5th district Rep. Patrick Michael “PM” Vargas filed House Bill No. 10306, which sought to tweak the 2001 law and strengthen public protection against charges that should not be passed on to citizens. The measure aligns with President Marcos' directive in his July 27 State of the Nation Address (SONA) to lower electricity costs and improve efficiency in the energy sector. Under the proposal, non-technical losses such as electricity theft and system deficiencies can no longer be charged to consumers. Only legitimate transmission and distribution losses may be included, subject to stricter and fairer limits. "Malinaw ang mensahe ng Pangulo—dapat gumaan ang pasanin ng mamamayan sa kuryente. Sa HB No.10306, tinatama natin ang matagal nang mali kung saan ang inefficiencies sa sistema ay ipinapasa pa sa konsyumer," Vargas said. (The President’s message is clear—electricity costs must be lighter for the people. With HB No.10306, we correct the long-standing injustice where system inefficiencies are passed on to consumers.) Currently, system loss charges form part of monthly electricity bills, allowing distribution utilities to recover lost energy in transmission and distribution. Vargas, a second-termer, insisted that citizens should not bear losses caused by negligence or illegal acts. "Hindi makatarungan na ang isang pamilyang Pilipino ay magbabayad para sa kuryenteng ninakaw o nasayang dahil sa kahinaan ng sistema. Panahon na para ilagay ang pananagutan kung saan ito nararapat," he noted. (It is unjust for Filipino families to pay for stolen or wasted electricity due to system weaknesses. It is time to place accountability where it belongs.) The bill also lowers and restructures the system loss cap to ensure that savings and operational efficiency directly benefit consumers in their electricity bills. According to Vargas, affordable electricity is vital not only for households but also for small businesses, education, and health services. Kung seryoso tayo sa layunin ng Pangulo na pababain ang gastos ng bawat pamilyang Pilipino, dapat nating simulan sa pagtanggal ng mga hindi makatarungang singil sa kuryente—at ito ang nangunguna nating isinusulong sa panukalang ito," said Quezon City lawmaker. (If we are serious about the President’s goal of reducing household expenses, we must start by removing unjust electricity charges—and this is what we are prioritizing in this proposal.) HB No. 10306 is expected to be discussed in the appropriate House committee in the coming weeks.

Australia backs fight against drug-resistant tuberculosis. Health security rarely makes headlines, but it remains one of the most practical forms of diplomacy. That was evident as healthcare professionals, tuberculosis specialists, and public health officials from seven Southeast Asian countries gathered in Makati City for a regional capacity-building program aimed at strengthening the fight against drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB). Organized by the PeerLINC Knowledge Hub in partnership with TB Alliance and the Tropical Disease Foundation (TDF), the four-day program was supported by the Australian Government through AusAID and brought together delegates from Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Timor-Leste, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Rather than focusing solely on scientific advances, the training emphasized something equally important: helping countries learn directly from one another as they adapt new treatment approaches to their own healthcare systems. Opening the program, Patrick Angeles, Program Officer for Health Partnerships at the Australian Embassy in the Philippines, highlighted the value of regional cooperation in addressing health challenges that do not recognize national borders. “This PeerLINC regional training is an important platform to exchange knowledge,” Angeles said. “We encourage participants to draw not only from the expertise of our resource persons and site visits, but also from each other’s successes and challenges.” He added that Australia’s development cooperation places strong emphasis on building lasting professional relationships, expressing hope that participants would leave with not only new technical knowledge but also a network of colleagues they could continue working with long after the training concluded. The initiative reflects Australia’s continuing support for strengthening health systems across the region through technical cooperation and knowledge sharing. That partnership has grown steadily in recent years. In 2025, Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade also supported a PeerLINC regional training involving delegates from Somalia and several Pacific Island countries, underscoring Australia’s broader commitment to improving regional preparedness against infectious diseases. Over four days, participants explored the implementation of newer, shorter, and more patient-centered treatment regimens for drug-resistant tuberculosis through technical discussions, clinical case exercises, cross-country exchanges, and field visits to health facilities in Makati and Pasay. The visits allowed delegates to observe how treatment protocols are applied beyond the classroom and within community health settings. For Michelle Goroh, a public health physician and tuberculosis program manager with Malaysia’s Sabah State Health Department, the opportunity to visit Philippine health facilities proved especially valuable. “We were able to assess the accessibility of health facilities, the availability of tests, the acceptability of BPaLM/BPaL regimens among patients, and the feasibility of implementing drug-resistant TB care in the Philippines,” she said. Dr. Eden Mendoza-Hisey, head of the PeerLINC Knowledge Hub, said the program was designed to help countries move beyond clinical evidence toward practical implementation. “When program leaders learn from peers who have already worked through similar challenges, they can adapt practical solutions more effectively and strengthen the care available to patients,” she said. The program concluded with each delegation developing country-specific action plans for the coming year, covering priorities in diagnostics, clinical care, patient support, and program management. While tuberculosis remains a national public health concern, controlling drug-resistant strains increasingly depends on countries sharing knowledge, experience, and practical solutions across borders. For Australia, supporting such initiatives represents another example of how development cooperation extends beyond financial assistance. It is equally about building the regional partnerships and professional networks needed to confront shared challenges together.

14 hurt in military crane crash in Sulu. ZAMBOANGA CITY – Fourteen persons were injured after a military crane crashed in Indanan, Sulu on Friday, July 31. Investigation said the crane from the 545th Engineering Brigade was travelling along Kilometer 2 in Barangay Kajatian when the driver lost control of the vehicle. The truck rammed two utility vehicles and three motorcycles and injured several civilians. The victims were taken to the Sulu Integrated Provincial Hospital. The 11th Infantry “Alakdan” Division expressed “deep concern for the injured civilians and wishes them a swift and full recovery.” The truck was enroute to support a mobile crane mission when it experienced a mechanical malfunction. Authorities are investigating the incident.

Hernandez, Sarines complete week of dominance at Pradera Verde. Jet Hernandez and Lisa Sarines put the finishing touches to an overpowering week for themselves, as the final round of the NGAP National Strokeplay Championship on Saturday, July 31, only confirmed how good they have been before formally taking home their respective men's and ladies' titles. The 21-year-old Hernandez closed out with a two-under-par 70 for a 72-hole 269 total, 19-under overall at the Pinatubo layout of Pradera Verde that completed a 22-stroke victory over fellow national pool members Chris Remata and Rolando Bregente, while Sarines submitted a 76 for a 15-shot win over Tashanah Balangauan. "I feel like the work that I have put in the last two years--the swing change and everything else--have really come to fruition," Hernandez, an incoming psychology senior at University of Denver, said. "I really came out today with a personal goal of going bogey-free. "But I had some misfortune on No. 14. That's golf and it is what it is," added Hernandez, who opened up with a bogeyless 65 on Wednesday and then broke away the following day with 10 birdies in a second straight 65 that set the tone of the rout. All told, Hernandez had 20 birdies and two eagles against just five bogeys in an overpowering display of scoring that establishes him as the solid choice to complete a golden double next week in the National Match Play Championship set at Luisita in Tarlac starting Tuesday. "I'm not hiding the fact that I also would want to win that, because I am a competitor," Hernandez said. "But that's a very different tournament. I have to get into the right mindset, prepare myself mentally for that." Remata cracked par for the first time this week, matching Hernandez' 70, to catch Bregente at 291 after Bregente closed out with three bogeys in his last five holes for a 74. Jacob Rolida was another two shots back also after a 74, with Jed Dy completing the top five at 295 after a final round 76. Sarines, meanwhile, basically coasted along to the win and turned in her coldest round of the week, which was marred by a double bogey on No. 15. Still, her win was so authoritative that no player in the lean field was able to outscore her on any round, with Balangauan and Precious Zaragosa firing matching 76s to round out the podium. Zaragosa, the 15-year-old playing out of Canlubang, finished five strokes behind Balangauan, with Jules Gaerlan and Crista Minoza coming in another six shots back also after shooting 76s.

Maynilad septic tank cleanup to cover selected Manila barangays in August. Maynilad Water Services, Inc. will deploy desludging trucks to selected barangays in Manila this August as part of its ongoing septic tank cleaning program. Areas included in the August schedule are Port Area, Quiapo, San Miguel, San Nicolas, Sta. Cruz, and Sta. Mesa. In an advisory, the company urged residents to check whether their barangay is included in the scheduled route through announcements on Maynilad’s official website and social media pages, as well as through coordination with their respective barangay offices. Maynilad said households qualify for the service if their septic tanks have not been desludged by the company within the last five years. For barangays included in the schedule, residents do not need to book an appointment as desludging teams will conduct house-to-house operations. Meanwhile, customers whose areas are not part of the August rollout but are due for septic tank cleaning may request the service by calling Hotline 1626 or by filling out an online request form: Maynilad desludging request form . Schedules will be confirmed after processing. Maynilad said it will strictly follow its monthly barangay schedule and reminded residents to take advantage of the service once it reaches their communities. The company added that the desludging program is part of its sanitation efforts and is already covered under customers’ regular water service fees.

OPAPRU keeps door open for CPP-NPA peace talks, cites gains from localized peace engagement. The national government remains open to resuming peace talks with the Communist Party of the Philippines – New People's Army – National Democratic Front (CPP-NPA-NDF) provided both sides share the same goal of achieving lasting peace without a “hidden agenda.” Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) Secretary Mel Senen S. Sarmiento said the Marcos administration continues to pursue peace despite focusing on ending insurgency on the ground. “Government has always been open to dialogue with anyone. The intention of government has never been in question because it is sincere,” he told reporters on Friday, July 31. “If the objective is to achieve peace, then those talking to government should be just as sincere. There should be no hidden agenda. Both sides should have the same agenda, which is to achieve genuine peace and focus on fighting only one enemy, poverty,” he added. In 2024, the OPAPRU had said that President Marcos Jr. remained optimistic a peace agreement with the CPP-NPA could still be pursued before the end of his term. Asked if he remains optimistic with less than two years left in the administration, Sarmiento pointed instead to conditions in former conflict areas. “When I go around the country, I do not rely only on data. I used to be DILG secretary and a local chief executive. I like talking to people. When I was mayor, I would sleep anywhere, walk eight to 10 hours through the mountains and stay in small bamboo houses,” he said. "What matters to me is whether people actually feel the change. They tell me places that used to be troubled are now peaceful. What they ask for now are roads and bridges. They feel that local governments are now working for them,” he continued. “With the help of the Armed Forces and the Philippine National Police, local officials can now reach communities they could not enter before because the fear brought by security threats is gone,” he added. He said reports from local officials continue to show former rebels surrendering, even as insurgency has yet to be completely eliminated. “There are still remnants but if you look at the numbers, they are already very small across the country. Just yesterday, local officials reported that more rebels had surrendered,” he said. Localized peace engagement Sarmiento said OPAPRU's experience shows that localized peace engagement has become one of the government's most effective approaches in encouraging rebels to return to the fold, which refers to a community-based approach to resolving local insurgency by letting local government units (LGUs) take the lead in engaging members and supporters of communist rebel groups in their respective areas. He said the strategy is rooted in existing laws and was reinforced by Executive Order No. 70, which institutionalized the whole-of-nation approach to ending local communist armed conflict. According to Sarmiento, the framework traces its foundation to the 1987 Constitution and the Local Government Code of 1991, which devolved powers to local governments. Under the law, governors and mayors are responsible for maintaining peace and order in their communities as chairpersons of local peace and order councils. They also supervise local police through authority delegated by the National Police Commission (Napolcom) and may call on the Armed Forces of the Philippines and other security agencies to respond to threats such as rebellion. “In reality, when the Local Government Code took effect in 1992, this became the responsibility of governors and mayors. It is no longer something that should be left to the President alone,” he said. He added that local executives also lead economic development in their areas, making it possible to pursue peace and development at the same time. “Some say peace must come before development. Others say development should come first. That cannot be the case. They should happen together,” he said. Sarmiento said local officials are more effective in persuading members of armed groups because they know the communities and families involved. “If they want to surrender, they are sometimes afraid to approach uniformed personnel because of things they have heard. But when they talk to their local leaders, governors or mayors, they become convinced. It has been very effective,” he said. He said the government sustains peace by bringing infrastructure and basic services into cleared communities through a whole-of-government approach, while civil society helps convince remaining rebels to abandon the armed struggle. Revitalized LPE Sarmiento also said OPAPRU has been reminding local governments to fully implement provisions of the Local Government Code requiring at least 25 percent representation from civil society organizations in local development councils. He said some former rebels are now in the process of selecting representatives to sit in municipal development councils. “Instead of taking up arms, they now advance their concerns through advocacy. They participate in the budgeting process and in preparing the annual investment plan of local governments,” he said. "We firmly believe government becomes more effective not by working for the people, but by working with the people. If government works with former rebels and other stakeholders, governance becomes more responsive and inclusive,” he added. Sarmiento said localized peace engagement is now being implemented in 59 provinces involving 26,692 former rebels. He added that 3,678 former rebel people's organizations have already been organized. “The people ask for only one thing, peace. We cannot allow conflict to continue in this country. Every gunshot is equivalent to half a kilo of rice. Money that should go to education, agriculture, and helping poor patients instead goes to buying bullets. That is why the government is very serious about achieving peace,” he said.

Moroccans sought better future in collective crossing to Spain territory. CEUTA, Spain (AP) – When he heard the border had been breached, Abdulah Buji jumped on his motorbike and raced from his home in northern Morocco towards Ceuta, joining thousands of people trying to swim into the tiny Spanish territory in North Africa. Like many of his fellow countrymen, Buji was inspired by the thought that this collective crossing could somehow unlock his dream of reaching Spain and starting a new life in Europe. “Spain gives you the chance to make your future, not like Morocco,” said Buji, a 21-year-old who is studying to be a teacher. “I am a talented boy. I just want a chance.” But his elation at setting foot on Spanish soil was quickly followed by the disheartening realization that he was still far from his ultimate goal. Mainland Europe rested across the Mediterranean, and he and the new arrivals were unwanted. Spanish authorities ordered everyone to turn around and go back or face eventual expulsion. Buji said he almost joined more than 50 people who died trying to reach Ceuta while swimming around a border fence. He made it across, but he lost his belongings and money in the crossing. When he realized that he would likely face legal limbo and detention, he turned around and headed back. “I’ve spent perhaps 14 years studying, but there’s nothing at home, and I’d have to work 12-hour shifts for a meager wage,” Buji told The Associated Press. “That’s why I came here, but I haven’t found any opportunities here either, so I have to go back.” Of the 60,000 people who crossed between Thursday and Friday morning, some 45,000 had returned to Moroccan territory within hours after many spent the night on the streets of Ceuta amid startled locals and armed Spanish police and soldiers. The massive influx of people, which totaled 70 percent of Ceuta’s resident population, sparked calls by local Spanish authorities for police and the army to establish order. Locals were concerned by the thousands of mostly young men aimlessly walking the streets. Ceuta’s residents recalled a similar but smaller migration crisis in 2021, when the Moroccan government dropped its border controls and let several thousand people from Morocco and sub-Saharan countries into Ceuta over two days. The city faced a much larger humanitarian crisis this time. As the first reports and videos of migrants reaching Ceuta spread on social media, more people headed north in hopes of reaching European Union territory. Train stations in Morocco’s capital, Rabat, and in the country’s largest city, Casablanca, were crowded with people trying to travel to the border with Ceuta. Local media showed police officers preventing some of them from boarding trains and buses. It isn’t clear what triggered the influx, but social media was awash with posts encouraging Moroccans to try to enter Ceuta days before it began, said Myriam Cherti, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford’s Center on Migration, Policy, and Society. The posts included practical information on how to cross the border and what migrants should say to increase their chances of being allowed to stay. Cherti said some of the migrants she interviewed over the past year had lost count of the number of times they had tried to cross the border. “They’re doing it out of despair, they’re doing it because they’ve tried other ways to build a life and failed, they’re doing it because they feel the obligation that they want to help their families and support them,” she said. “And that’s possible if they make it to Spain and not necessarily possible if they stay” in Morocco. Ahmed Karim, 33, was among those who managed to cross into Ceuta. He doesn't have work and says the problem is compounded for many Moroccans due to the difficulty in traveling outside the country. He said many Moroccans want to go to Europe or America, “but they don’t have the opportunity.” Other people who crossed, however, were not coming to stay; they were searching for lost loved ones and hoping they were not among the dead. Ikrra Khai, 33, is one of thousands of Moroccan women who regularly get temporary job permits to work on Spanish farms at harvest time. On Friday, she was in Ceuta looking for the brother of a good friend. “I don’t know if he is dead or alive,” she said. “I have his residency card. But I don’t know where he is. I’m searching.”

Fever's Cunningham unfazed by 'distraction' label. PORTLAND, Oregon (AP) — Sophie Cunningham says she's unconcerned that the rallies against transgender participation in women's sports that have accompanied the Indiana's Fever's recent games are a distraction for the WNBA team. Cunningham made the comments before the Fever's game Friday night, July 31, against the Portland Fire. Outside, a group rallied for the second straight game in support of Cunningham and her recent comments about transgender athletes. “I think at the end of the day, I come in and I do my job,” Cunningham said. "I think everyone who knows me personally, they know that I’m full of love. I’m bubbly. I love the people around me. I love basketball. I love inspiring the next generation and doing that in a positive light. And so that doesn’t even cross my mind. Doesn’t cross my teammates’ minds. “And again, I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me, and I’m not gonna like shadow that or hide or, you know, dim my light just because maybe people don’t agree with that.” Portland's rally came after a similar rally for Cunningham earlier in the week before the Fever's game at the Seattle Storm. Both rallies only attracted about two dozen participants and a bevy of onlookers. “I have honestly had nothing to do with them,” Cunningham said. “I think it’s people just practicing their rights of freedom of speech and doing what other fans have been doing since the WNBA has started. And so props to them, props to everyone who is able to be competent and be bold and courageous enough to to speak their truths.” Another rally was planned for Sunday in Minneapolis when the Fever play the Minnesota Lynx. In Seattle on Tuesday, two Cunningham supporters sat courtside at Climate Change Arena holding signs. A co-owner of the Storm, Celeste Keaton was later fined an undisclosed amount and suspended for five games by the WNBA for an exchange with the two supporters. The Storm also apologized for the incident, but did not provide details about the exchange, releasing a statement that said: “We remain committed to creating a welcoming and respectful environment for anyone who attends a Storm game.” The Seattle rally promoted statewide ballot initiative, IL26-638, that would bar transgender students from participating in girls’ athletics at Washington schools. It also praised Cunningham, who voiced support for barring transgender athletes from girls’ and women’s sports in recent interviews. “I am here to be a cheerleader for Sophie Cunningham, who has so bravely put her head above the parapet to protect women and girls in our sports and in our locker rooms,” said Amy Souza, who was among those at the Portland rally. “I was an organizer of this event, I was a co-organizer of the Seattle event. I’m also here, standing in solidarity with those teen girls who, unfortunately, were harassed when they were just trying to be fans of the sport, fans of Sophie Cunningham.” Cunningham was booed by the Moda Center crowd in Portland when she entered the game midway though the first quarter. Many waved small pink, blue and white transgender flags. The Fever downed the Fire 112-98 for their fifth straight win. Cunningham finished with 13 points and Caitlin Clark had her fourth career triple-double with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Coach Stephanie White said she was concerned that the controversy was distracting from the team's play. “You know there is a frustration, of course, because we want to we want to talk about basketball and we want to continue to work on our game and we want to continue to grow as a team.,” White said. “But I also understand this is part of our growth edge as a league, right? It’s part of our growth as a league, and we have to to be able to manage, we have to be able to insulate as much as we can, and then we have to be able to lead with conversation.”

‘Part of the battle’: Ombudsman Remulla says Revilla bail ruling was expected. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said on Saturday, Aug. 1, that the Sandiganbayan’s decision granting bail to former senator Ramon “Bong” Revilla Jr. in his pending malversation case involving the alleged anomalous P92.8-million flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan was “part of the battle” and an outcome the Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) had anticipated. “Hinihintay ng tao kung ano'ng reaction ko sa bail. Well, it’s just part of the battle. Alam mo, we are fighting a big war, it’s just one battle (People have been waiting for my reaction to the bail. Well, it’s just part of the battle. You know, we are fighting a big war; this is just one battle),” he said in his radio program at DZRH. “We can afford to lose a battle. We lost this battle. We predicted this to happen… I was mentioning this in one of our lunches na mangyayari ‘yan (this will happen). Mayroon talagang mangyayari na mukhang tinatrabaho, na magkakaroon ng grant of bail (There were indeed indications that things were being worked on that would result in the grant of bail),” he added. Remulla said the decision in that particular battle may have been different, but maintained that the OMB and advocates of reform believe corruption can only be addressed through a whole-of-government approach. “Kami sa Ombudsman, we raise the standard of reasonable certainty of conviction before we file a case. Tinaas na namin ang standard. Hindi ito weaponized. Evidence-based (At the Office of the Ombudsman, we have raised the standard of reasonable certainty of conviction before we file a case. We have raised that standard. This is not weaponized. It is evidence-based),” he went on. He said the OMB cannot wage the fight against corruption alone, noting that the judiciary plays an equally important role. According to Remulla, he would soon seek a dialogue with the Supreme Court (SC) and would contact his classmate after the program to set up a meeting. “I want to talk with the Chief Justice [Alexander Gesmundo] who’ll be retiring in November so his legacy will be okay, will be good. It takes a whole-of-government approach to solve this. Ang kalahati ng proseso ang judiciary (The judiciary is half of the process),” he said. In a resolution penned by Associate Justice Fritz Bryn Anthony M. Delos Santos, the anti-graft court’s Third Division on July 31 granted bail to Revilla but denied the bail applications of his co-accused, all officials of the DPWH Bulacan 1st District Engineering Office (DEO). On the same day, Revilla posted the P1-million cash bail required by the anti-graft court. Prior to posting bail, the former senator was detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Barangay Payatas.

9 dead as Russia pounds Kyiv with ballistic missiles. KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia launched an intense barrage of ballistic missiles and drones overnight into Saturday, killing at least nine people and injuring 22 civilians in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, Ukrainian authorities said. The strikes came two days after a major Russian attack killed at least 10 people and injured more than 50 others across Ukraine, as Moscow apparently looks to exploit Kyiv’s critical shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defenses. The relentless cycle of attacks dims the potential of reaching a diplomatic end to Russia’s more than four-year-old invasion of its neighbor. Russia’s defense ministry said Saturday it had launched a “massive strike” against “Ukrainian military-industrial complex facilities and logistics centers in Kyiv.” A five-story residential building in the city's Solomianskyi District was damaged by falling debris and a fire broke out. Rescue workers evacuated 35 people from the upper floors of the building and two people died, with eight reported injured, including two children, according to Ukraine’s state emergency service. In the Darnytskyi District of Kyiv, seven people were killed and another 14 injured after the attack caused fires and damage to houses, vehicles, an administrative and non-residential building, the emergency services said. Elsewhere, emergency workers extinguished a fire in a non-residential building in the capital’s Shevchenkivskyi district. There was no additional information about earlier reports by the district mayor that people were trapped in another residential building. Damage to commercial and residential buildings was reported in two other city districts. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has pressed the United States and other Western partners over Ukraine’s need for more Patriot anti-ballistic missile defense systems to counter missile attacks from Russia. The Ukrainian leader late Friday said he spoke to US Vice President JD Vance and discussed a meeting with President Donald Trump earlier this week in Washington, which Zelenskyy described as “positive and productive.” “The Russian air strikes on our country continue and air defense, specifically interceptors for Patriot systems against ballistic missiles, remains a top priority,” Zelenskyy said Friday in a post on Telegram. At a NATO summit in Ankara in July, Trump said the US would give Ukraine a license to make Patriot systems, but he appeared to move away from that commitment on Friday during a Cabinet meeting at the presidential retreat in Camp David, Maryland, saying he had not yet made a final decision on the matter. From a basement shelter where she was taking cover as a second air alarm sounded for another wave, Liudmyla Nakonechna, 64, described how she was woken by loud explosions at 1:30 a.m. “I ran into the corridor and was standing there when the bathroom door was blown off its hinges and struck me in the leg,” said Nakonechna, whose health is poor after undergoing cancer treatment. “I heard the sound of shattering glass. My balcony was covered in glass and it was completely blown apart, while the windows in my bedroom were also blown out.” Nakonechna had not taken cover in a shelter since Russia’s full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, but the stress became too much, she said. “It’s getting worse by the day,” Nakonechna said. “Whereas before there was an attack once every two weeks, or maybe once a week, now it happens practically every day. It is incredibly hard to bear this psychologically.”

Alas Girls brace for FIVB U17 World Championship test.
