Dengue cases in Cebu rising. CEBU CITY – Persistent rainy days bring a rising risk of dengue, authorities warned Saturday. The Cebu provincial government has intensified its dengue response by activating hospital measures to ensure faster assessment and treatment of suspected dengue cases. With 381 confirmed cases across the province in July, the Provincial Health Office (PHO) reported that dengue infections are rising. “There is a spike considering that we're in the rainy season," Dr. Jenina Canoy, Provincial Health Officer 1, said. Canoy said dengue fast lanes in all 16 Capitol-run provincial and district hospitals have been activated. Capitol health consultant Dr. Nikki Catalan said there is no dengue outbreak in the province but the increasing cases require close monitoring. “We'd stay guarded. We cannot call it an outbreak but just of concern because of the rise of the cases,” Catalan told reporters. PHO data showed that Toledo City recorded the highest number of dengue cases with 49, followed by Barili with 39, Talisay City with 34, Consolacion with 33, and Carcar City and Medellin with 19 cases each. Other areas with dengue cases were Cordova and Dalaguete with 17 cases each, Sogod with 14, Danao City with 13, and Argao, Balamban, and Compostela with 12 cases each. "In the past three months, dengue cases have really increased,” Catalan added. Through the fast lane system, waiting time will be shortened with patients receiving immediate assessment, quicker laboratory testing, closer monitoring, and early medical intervention.

Earthquake survivors in Japan sleep in cars in sweltering heat. YATSUSHIRO, Japan (AP) – Thousands of survivors of a powerful earthquake in southwestern Japan spent Friday in crowded shelters or sleeping in cars as they faced shortages of water and fuel and punishing summer temperatures that stoked fears of heat-related illness. The death toll rose to 34, the Kumamoto prefectural government said, as rescuers raced to find those still missing after the quake triggered a mall explosion, toppled a factory chimney, and flattened homes. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stressed that authorities must secure water supplies by doing “whatever it takes” and called for close coordination with the military and other relevant agencies. The earthquake left thousands of homes without power, but electricity was fully restored by Friday evening. The local power company also said there were no immediate reports of remaining outages. The magnitude-7.1 earthquake hit Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu on Tuesday. As search operations entered a fourth day, it wasn’t known how many people remained missing. More than 1,500 buildings were damaged, including 179 that were destroyed, according to preliminary assessments by Kumamoto officials. Officials said one more death and its connection to the quake is under investigation. At least 96 people were injured, including six seriously. In Yatsushiro City, another hard-hit area in southern Kumamoto, Kinparo, a 116-year old Japanese inn, was severely damaged, with its roofed main entrance collapsed to the ground, white walls cracked and rooftiles fell. On Friday, three days after the quake, workers were removing parts of the gate, which is part of a registered historic property that needs to be restored. Started in 1910, the three-story ryokan with traditional architecture and its hot bath have attracted many fans from the region and across Japan. “The damage is tremendous and it would require significant repairs, and I can’t even think if or how I can do that,” inn owner Keisuke Matsumoto said. “But it’s a valuable family inn that has been handed down for generations since my great-great grandfather built it, so I do hope to preserve it.” Inside, his mother Misao Matsumoto said she was not injured in the quake but “I’m mentally discouraged. It’s very painful to see parts of what I’ve lived with and enjoyed for decades crumble to that state.” But she said experts of historic buildings will come in to discuss the reconstruction, so “I have to hang in there.” Across the street from the Kinparo inn, a fish cake shop owner unable to resume his business due to the water cutoff was giving away tube-shaped fish cakes while they are still edible. Signs for the “chikuwa” fish cake hang from the ceiling. “I just wanted to cheer up this neighborhood,” said shop owner Shinichiro Katayama. He says he cannot clean or check his fish cake machine is intact until the water supply resumes. “I don’t even know if the machine still works. When water supply is back that would be my first step toward a recovery.” Kumamoto authorities said nearly 80,000 homes remained without water. More than 9,000 people were staying in shelters, where power sources were being added to provide air conditioning. Fuel has also become scarce as power outages disabled gas stations and quake damage disrupted deliveries from other regions. Many have resorted to sleeping in their cars for privacy, but with the fuel shortage, they struggle to keep the air conditioning running in sweltering temperatures. Japan's weather agency and the Ministry of the Environment issued an extreme heat alert for Kumamoto city Friday as temperatures peaked at 36 C (97 F). Hirokazu Sato, who lost his home in the earthquake, said he and his wife and three children would remain in their car until they can move into temporary housing. “I don’t know how soon I’d be able to move in,” said Sato. “We need to have the air conditioning on throughout the day and night, which uses up gas.” Kumamoto is also a major industrial hub, and there are concerns that the quake could possibly disrupt semiconductor and auto-parts supply chains for months to come. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, a global chip giant that operates a lab in Kumamoto, said all personnel were safe and operations were gradually resuming after postquake inspections found the structure was sound, although detailed inspections and impact assessments were still underway. Japanese officials had described Friday afternoon as a crucial point for rescue efforts as some experts say survival chances decline after the first three days. With search dogs, rescuers continued looking for survivors across the Kumamoto area, including at the collapsed Aeon Mall in the town of Kashima, one of the hardest-hit sites. The complex was bustling with thousands of people when the quake happened. The company said about 3,000 shoppers were evacuated to a parking lot before an explosion happened in another part of the mall, where some staff remained working. The mall’s second floor collapsed, trapping people. Seven of the 11 rescued were confirmed dead, but officials did not say if anyone else is missing. A search operation had ended at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in the Yatsushiro city where a chimney collapsed in the quake, officials said. Of the 11 people dug out there, nine were confirmed dead. Smaller-scale searches continued Friday at the sites of collapsed houses in badly hit towns in southern Kumamoto. Authorities haven't supplied a firm figure for how many people are missing.

Pro tips for mastering Prada Beauty's viral Touch Cream-to-Powder Blush. Recently, Zendaya's ethereal glow at the red carpet premiere of “The Odyssey” sent beauty enthusiasts into detective mode. The answer behind her fresh, softly sculpted cheeks was later revealed by makeup artist Ernesto Casillas: Prada Beauty's newest Touch Cream-to-Powder Blush. For Filipino beauty lovers, recreating that coveted flush no longer requires waiting for an overseas release. Prada Touch has officially landed at Prada Beauty's flagship store in Greenbelt 5. To celebrate its arrival, the luxury beauty brand hosted a masterclass on July 31 led by celebrity makeup artist Janica Cleto, who shared practical techniques for getting the most out of the product, from choosing the right shade to making it last in the country's humid weather. A cream that finishes like powder Prada Touch introduces a cream-to-powder formula that melts into the skin before setting into a soft matte finish. The blush combines the blendability of a cream with the wear of a powder while remaining buildable, allowing users to go from a subtle flush to a more sculpted look. It is also designed as a multi-use product that can be applied on the cheeks, lips, and eyes for an easy monochromatic makeup look. Janica demonstrated exactly that during the masterclass, using the blush not only on the cheeks but also on the model's eyelids and lips for a fresh, coordinated finish. She advised applying the product with fingers instead of a brush. "The best way to apply it will be using your hands or your fingers," she said, explaining that the formula blends seamlessly with the warmth of the skin and allows users to gradually build the intensity instead of applying too much at once. The packaging has a hidden purpose Beyond its pocket-sized triangular compact inspired by the brand’s iconic logo, she revealed that the packaging doubles as a makeup guide. She introduced Prada's "triangle gestures," showing how the compact can help map blush placement depending on the desired effect. Positioning the triangle higher on the cheek creates a lifted, sculpted appearance, while placing it lower gives a softer, more romantic flush. The compact also features a stackable design, allowing multiple shades to connect together for easy, on-the-go use. Layer, don't overload For those worried about cream blush fading in tropical weather, Janica recommended saving one final layer for the end of the routine. She explained that complexion products like concealer and powder can slightly soften the blush's appearance, so after setting the makeup, adding another light layer helps refresh the color and extend its wear. She also encouraged users not to be afraid of layering. "It's always better to layer," she said, noting that the formula remains blendable even after multiple applications, making it easier to control the intensity without looking heavy. Shades that flatter morena skin Among Prada Touch's eight shades, Janica recommends P71 Bow for morena complexions. Despite appearing as a nude brown in the pan, she said it leaves behind a natural pink flush that complements warmer skin tones. For those willing to try bolder colors, she also recommends R68 Cherry. Although its bright red pan can seem intimidating, she said red mimics the skin's natural flush, making it surprisingly flattering across different complexions. She added that because Prada Touch is highly blendable and buildable, users can simply start with a light tap of the product and gradually layer until they achieve their desired look. As Prada Beauty continues to expand its makeup line, the brand is also strengthening its roster of global faces. While model Bella Hadid fronts the new Prada Touch campaign as the brand's first global beauty ambassador, actress Zendaya names the face of Prada Paradoxe fragrance. Together, the two ambassadors represent Prada Beauty's vision of individuality and modern self-expression, whether through a signature scent or a touch of color.

Third Filipino seafarer dies in Black Sea attacks as DMW halts deployment to danger zone. The death toll among Filipino seafarers caught in attacks on commercial ships in the northern Black Sea has risen to three as the government stepped up repatriation efforts and barred deployment to the conflict zone, Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said on Saturday, Aug. 1. Cacdac said the latest fatality was among Filipino crew members aboard ships that came under attack while docked at Ukrainian ports. “Last week, we reported two deceased. Today, I am reporting that there is one additional fatality. We now have three Filipinos who died in the northern Black Sea attacks on ships docked in Ukrainian ports. We also have one missing,” he said during the Saturday News Forum. The attacks stemmed from the escalating hostilities in the region as Cacdac said Ukraine attacked Russia in the Sea of Azov, prompting Russian strikes on Ukraine, including ports where commercial vessels with Filipino crew members were docked. The DMW said 17 ships carrying Filipino seafarers have been attacked over the past three weeks. A total of 236 Filipino seafarers were on board the affected vessels. Of the number, 217 escaped unharmed while 15 were injured. Cacdac said 89 seafarers have already been repatriated, including nine of the 15 injured crew members. “Six injured seafarers remain overseas. The others have already been taken off the ships and are now in different locations in Ukraine, Romania, Greece, and Turkey,” he said. Tragic homecoming The DMW chief said the government is now arranging the return of the remains of the three deceased seafarers. “We are working with the shipowners, the Department of Foreign Affairs, and the manning agencies to ensure their immediate repatriation,” Cacdac said. He said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered the DMW to extend full assistance to the victims' families. “Following the President's instructions, I personally visited the families of the three deceased, including the family of the missing seafarer. I conveyed the President's sympathies and his directive to provide full support and assistance,” Cacdac said. He also announced that he and Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Administrator Patricia Yvonne "PY" Caunan will leave for Romania on Monday to meet Filipino seafarers brought there after the attacks. “One of the human remains is in Romania. We will visit the morgue where the remains are being kept,” he said. The trip will be coordinated with the DFA and the Philippine Embassy in Bucharest headed by Ambassador Noel Servigon. Dangerous times Amid the continuing violence, the DMW has directed licensed manning agencies and shipowners to stop sending Filipino seafarers to the northern Black Sea. Cacdac said the DMW also ordered the immediate repatriation of Filipino crew members from attacked vessels and instructed shipowners to move 180 other Filipino seafarers aboard 12 ships that have not been attacked to safer ports. “We have directed all manning agencies not to allow ships carrying Filipino seafarers to proceed to the northern Black Sea because we received security assessments from the DFA and the Department of National Defense,” he said. "They have established that there is a full-scale international armed conflict in the area. The level of danger is very high. That is why there should be no Filipino seafarers there for now,” he added.

Veteran journalist Julius Segovia shares newsroom experiences in his first self-published workbook. For those who grew up watching the news on television, he was the familiar chinito reporter delivering stories for GMA News under the name Julius Segovia. For many of his students, however, he is simply Sir Julius, the mentor who generously shares lessons from the newsroom with aspiring journalists eager to enter one of the country's most demanding professions. Now, his more than two decades of experience in Philippine media are finding a new audience beyond the classroom. Julius has turned years of reporting, teaching, and mentoring into “Eere Tayo! A Practical Workbook for Journalism, Broadcasting and Digital Media,” a self-published learning resource set for release this September. In an interview with Manila Bulletin Lifestyle, Julius said the idea for the workbook grew from years of training campus journalists and school paper advisers in journalism competitions across the country. "Through the years, I noticed the limited availability of reference materials suited for Filipino students and the Philippine media setting," he said. "This inspired me to create a workbook that is more relatable, practical, conversational, and easy to understand for both students and teachers." Having spent more than 20 years in the media industry and over a decade in academia, he wanted to go beyond teaching theories and technical concepts. Instead, he packed the workbook with newsroom experiences, industry insights, and lessons drawn from both his successes and mistakes in the field. The workbook aims to bridge classroom instruction with real newsroom practice through practical exercises, newsroom simulations, reflection activities, and QR codes that link readers to actual news reports and broadcasting demonstrations. Students can also sharpen skills in reporting, scriptwriting, anchoring, interviewing, and storytelling through structured activities designed for classroom or independent learning. For him, learning directly from media practitioners gives students an advantage that textbooks alone cannot provide. "As a campus journalist, learning from a media practitioner is more than just something to be proud of. It is an opportunity to gain insights grounded in real-world experience," he said. "The lessons shared by someone who has worked in the industry go beyond theories found in books. They are practical, relevant, and tested in actual newsroom situations." Beyond technical skills, the workbook also includes insights and messages from fellow media practitioners, newsroom professionals, mentors, and industry colleagues to give readers a broader perspective on the profession. He hopes the book will become more than just another classroom reference. "I wanted this workbook to become an experiential learning material, one that would help students become familiar with the realities, challenges, pressures, and fast-paced environment of the real world of media and broadcasting," he said. Julius also considers the project part of his legacy as an educator and journalist, hoping it will continue guiding future generations of storytellers. "So, to every aspiring storyteller and communicator reading this workbook, welcome to the world of broadcasting. Hang on. The story is just getting started."

Loon reunites with Ozar, Nolasco in UP. Fil-American guard Ashley Loon is set for a reunion with Louna Ozar and Camille Nolasco after committing to University of the Philippines ahead of the UAAP Season 89 women’s basketball tournament in September. Loon, 21, joins the Maroons as a one-and-done player, reuniting with her former Gilas Pilipinas U18 teammates as UP looks to build on a disappointing Season 88 campaign that saw them finish seventh with a 3-11 win-loss record. Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. CALABRIA: SALVIAMO LO SCOGLIO DEL DELFINO. Ad Africo(prov. di Reggio Calabria) e dintorni tutta la popolazione si sta mobilitando per salvare il famosissimo "Scoglio del Delfino" sita nelle mitiche scogliere di Africo. L'iniziativa è stata promossa dalle varie associazioni nazionali e internazionali affinché l'erosione calcarea e la stupidità d alcuni turisti non rovini questa meravigliosa forma d'arte scultorea che Madre Natura ci ha regalato. A causa di alcuni turisti col vizio di staccare, armati d martelletto, pezzi di roccia da portare a casa come souvenir, la parte anteriore dello Scoglio del Delfino è profondamente lesionata. E come se non bastasse, anche pescatori d frodo muniti di bombole e scalpello stanno minando le fondamenta a caccia di avalloni e datteri di mare. Per questo bisogna salvarla con un intervento di messa in sicurezza serio e risolutore.

ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
